祭司那空洞的双眼微眯着，一时间纹丝不动。"不，" 他的声音化为电波，穿破了星际介质，染上一丝温暖的味道，"死者是数之不尽的。" 言罢，他的身形也随之颓落。

然后，随着一声低语，他转身走去，似乎期待着你跟上他。

texts.en: Moving deeper, between rooms and hulls, you witness galleries of the dead, bones and skulls carefully and artfully piled. You catch a glimpse now and then of pilgrims in ones and twos by their active vacsuit indicators. The curate leaves them to their contemplations.
texts.zh: 随着脚步逐渐深入，在那些房间和船体之中，你目睹了逝者的长廊，遗骸与头颅被精心而富有艺术感地堆积起来。通过真空服上那些激活的指示灯，你时不时可以瞥见三三两两的朝圣者。祭司没有打搅他们的深思。

texts.en:
"They are forgotten," the curate says, his gaze passing across the bones. Taking stock, somehow. "But I will not forget them. And all who visit here, they will help me remember that those who died may live eternal."

He fixes you now with a suddenly-piercing gaze, "You will help?"
texts.zh:
"他们已被遗忘，" 祭司说到，他的目光掠过这些遗骨，像是以某种方式在盘点着，"但我不会忘记。每一位造访此地的人，都会助我铭记 —— 这些逝者永垂不朽。"

而现在，他突然以一种锐利的目光凝视着你，"你也会帮我吗？"

options.en: I will fight to avenge them.

texts.en:
The curate sacraria stops before a pedestal, a bouquet of spines topped by fragments of skull. You see the glint of a cranial implant among the shards. The curate carefully lifts a fragment, trailing gold wire.

"Death comes for all. Every warlord, High Hegemon, CEO, spacer. Every prophet, every thief, every friend."

He looks at you with suddenly-piercing eyes, "Even you star-farer, fleet-captain. Death will come."
texts.zh:
神龛祭司在一个底座面前停下，底座上立着一束脊椎，顶端缀有颅骨的碎片，你甚至还能看见上面闪闪发亮的颅骨植入物。祭司小心翼翼地举起一块碎片，其后牵着一根金线。

"人终有一死。不论是军阀、至高霸主、CEO，还是宇宙民。所有先知，所有窃贼，所有友人。"

他的目光倏忽间刺向了你，"哪怕是你 ，身为远行者，身为舰队的舰长。死亡终将降临。"

options.en: Is that some kind of threat?

texts.en:
"They are forgotten," he says, "All forgotten, turned to dust by war. But I will remember that they once were. It is all I have to give."

The curate's suit helmet bobs at you, "And you will remember too, now."

"And then they shall live eternal. You understand?"
texts.zh:
"他们已被遗忘，" 他说到，"被世人尽数忘却，被战乱碾作飞灰。但我将铭记他们的存在，这正是我所必须付出的。"

祭司的服具头盔冲你低了低，"而现在，你也会铭记。"

"如此，他们将永垂不朽。你可明白？"

options.en: I will fight to avenge them.

texts.en:
He stops and fixes you with a suddenly piercing gaze. "The bodies, the bodies can be counted. Dust and bones."

"But not the dead. Their love, their life. No number remembers that." A pause. "You understand?"
texts.zh:
他停下来，你感受到如同锋刃一般的目光向你投来。"尸体，我们可以数清尸体。皆是尘埃与白骨。"

"但永远无法衡量死亡。他们的爱，他们的生命。没有数字能够记住那一切。" 他顿了顿，"你可明白？"

texts.en:
"Yes," the curate says, and brings a hand down to squeeze your shoulder, "Yes," he says again, and you can hear the smile in his voice.

Then, without a word, he disappears into some shadowy corridor.
texts.zh:
"是的，" 祭司说道，他伸出一只手拍了拍你的肩膀，"是的，" 他重复着，你能感受到他的声音中的笑意。

随后，他无声地隐入了某个昏暗的小道。

texts.en:
The curate thinks for a moment, then comes to a conclusion. "You will," he says, and brings a hand down to squeeze your shoulder, "Yes," he says again, and you can hear the start of a smile in his voice.

Then, without a word, he disappears into some shadowy corridor.
texts.zh:
祭司思索片刻便有了结论。"你会的，" 他说，并伸手拍了拍你的肩膀。"你会的，" 他重复道，你可以感受到他声音中的笑意。

随后，他无声地隐入了某个昏暗的小道。

texts.en:
The curate simply looks at you, then, you think, shakes his head. "Contemplate," he says finally.

With that said, and nothing else, he disappears into some shadowy corridor.
texts.zh:
祭司只是看着你，你好像看到他摇了摇头"请三思，" 他最终开口道。

说完，他便无声地隐入了某个昏暗的小道。

texts.en: You are left among the dead. The webs of ash hanging in the air twitch and flow as movement elsewhere in the labyrinth triggers minor fluctuations in the standing electrostatic charge.
texts.zh: 你被留在了茫茫死者之中。这幽幽曲径间的静电荷经久不散，每当它们产生一丝微不可查的涨落，空中悬浮的灰烬便如水网般流转不息。

texts.en:
You stay a while in the ossuary of Killa.

The hollow eyes keep silent vigil. Stacks and wings and arches and forests of human bone adorn every surface.

The dust-flux pulses slowly, like the breath of a titanic creature.
texts.zh:
你在 Killa 的藏骨堂稍作停留。

这些空洞的眼孔，彻夜不眠地进行着他们那永不停歇的祷告。书库，侧厅，拱门，森森白骨如林，装点着每一片角落。

尘埃之流缓缓搏动，有如庞然大物吞吐的气息。

texts.en:
Veils of dust slowly flex and twist in the electrostatic fields of the shrine, strong enough to overcome the low gravity of this world to hang in the near-vacuum.

Instructions are given by some unnamed Luddic priest who recites their words into crude repeaters awoken by your activity:

"Come only in peace. Let rest the dead. We pray now in the words revealed to Ludd... "
texts.zh:
尘埃如面纱一般在圣地的静电场中飘摇，电场的强度足以克服这颗星球微弱的引力，使尘埃悬浮在近乎真空的环境中。

你激活了简陋的中继器，一位不知名的卢德神父所朗诵的导言开始广播：

"铸剑为犁，逝者安息。我等虔诚祷告，谨遵卢德神启..."

texts.en:
In the gloom you begin to make out empty sockets, rib-cages, countless femurs and spines. They cluster in recesses, corners, in stowage spaces, their hatches removed.

Recorded verse haunt the comms channels.

"... cities fall from orbit like burning leaves / caught by the wind and wailing / life's breath pulled from mother and child..."
texts.zh:
在一片幽暗中，你渐渐辨认出空洞的眼窝，肋骨架，以及数之不尽的股骨和脊椎，它们一团团簇拥在壁龛里，在墙角里，在拆掉舱门的储物间里。

阴魂不散的诗篇，回荡在通信频道之中。

"...城塞，于星轨坠入凡尘，似落叶燎作飞灰 / 狂风无尽之哭嚎，困我于囹圄之中 / 母子相依为命，生息俱为所夺..."

texts.en:
Wandering the halls, you eventually encounter the curate sacraria of the ossuary. He is, as before, a man of few words, and greets you with only a nod and the ghost of a sad smile.

You are left among the dead. The webs of ash hanging in the air twitch and flow as movement elsewhere in the labyrinth trigger minor fluctuations in the standing electrostatic charge.
texts.zh:
在回廊中游荡着，你终于遇见了藏骨堂的神龛祭司。他一如往常，寡言少语，如幽灵般哀伤地微笑着，对你微微颔首致意。

你被留在了茫茫死者之中。这幽幽曲径间的静电荷经久不散，每当它们产生一丝微不可查的涨落，空中悬浮的灰烬便如水网般流转不息。

texts.en:
You leave the dead in their tombs within the battered crust of the lifeless moon below.

The flight in your return shuttle is uneventful.
texts.zh:
你留逝者安息于陵墓中，深埋在这死寂卫星那破碎的地壳之下。

搭乘穿梭机返航的过程一切顺利。

texts.en:
You leave the dead in their tombs within the battered crust of the lifeless moon below.

The flight in your return shuttle is uneventful.
texts.zh:
你留逝者安息于陵墓中，深埋在这死寂卫星那破碎的地壳之下。

搭乘穿梭机返航的过程一切顺利。

texts.en:
The concourse is in chaos. A crowd of protestors in Luddic greens has formed a human barrier across the main entrance. Surrounding them are angry spacers, officers and crew alike, waiting to enter the commercial promenade or return to their ships.

A small contingent of local MuniSec holds the shouting crowds apart - barely.
texts.zh:
港区陷入了一片混乱，一群身着卢德绿袍的抗议者在主要出入口形成了人墙。周遭堵满了想要进入商业街或返回舰船的宇宙民、军官与船员，他们现在怒气冲天。

一支地方安全部的小分队勉强把喧闹的人群隔开。

texts.en:
You recognize the Hegemony $post, $name speaking orders into a small comms unit. $HeOrShe notices you, and nods you over.

"Luddics protesting the planet-side burns," $heOrShe explains. "Get these every other week due to the pilgrims. They consider it a sort of rite of passage."

$HeOrShe one-arm shrugs to suggest that $heOrShe doesn't find the matter worth getting too upset over, then speaks another string of tactical jargon into $hisOrHer comms.
texts.zh:
你认出了那个霸主 $post，$name 正通过一个小型通讯器下达着命令。$HeOrShe注意到了你，并向你点头示意。

"卢德教徒正在抗议轨道焚化。" $HeOrShe解释说，"由于朝圣者的原因，这种事情每隔一周就会发生一次。他们都把这当成朝圣之路上的某种仪式了。"

$HeOrShe耸了耸半边肩膀，一副这事也不值得让$HeOrShe太上心的样子。随后$hisOrHer对着通讯器又说了一串战术术语。

options.en: Pilgrims? Is there some kind of shrine here?
options.zh: 朝圣者？这附近有圣地吗？

options.en: Use your commission with the Hegemony to pass
options.zh: 利用你与霸主的雇佣关系来通过这里

options.en: Use your standing with the Church to pass
options.zh: 利用你与教会的关系来通过这里

options.en: Wait for the authorities to clear the protest
options.zh: 等待当局驱散抗议人群

options.en: Join the protestors, help them take a stand
options.zh: 加入抗议者，帮他们表明立场

options.en: Offer your marines to help clear the protest
options.zh: 派遣你的陆战队员辅助当局驱散抗议者

options.en: Use your marines to muscle through right now
options.zh: 派遣你的陆战队员强行开路

texts.en:
"Not here," $heOrShe says, eyes not leaving the protestors. "On the surface. For appreciating the local plant-life. Don't understand why, you wouldn't believe how toxic the stuff is. Detox after exposure is like a week of hangover compressed down into a day or two."

$HeOrShe shakes $hisOrHer head. "At least that's what it felt like for me. Guess they like suffering. Luddics for you. Top brass says we gotta humor 'em. Politics, right?"

A burst of coded garble comes through the comms, and the $post gives a short response. "Gendarmerie will be here soon if you want to stay for the show," $heOrShe says.
texts.zh:
"有，不过不在这里，" $heOrShe说，视线并没有离开抗议者，"是在地表上，朝圣者们喜欢在那欣赏当地的植物。我不理解。你想象不到那些玩意的毒性有多强。人体暴露在那种环境中后，后续的排毒过程十分痛苦，好比是把整整一周的宿醉压缩到一至两天。"

$HeOrShe摇了摇头。"反正我的亲身体验就是这样的。可能这帮人就是喜欢受苦吧。这就是卢德信徒。上面的人说我们必须迁就他们。这就是政治，对吧？"

通讯器中传来一阵噪声，$post给出了一个简短的回答。"如果你想看看接下来会发生什么，宪兵马上就到了。" $heOrShe说。

texts.en: Suddenly the $rank does a double-take. "$playerName? That's you, isn't it? Commissioned Auxiliary, right? Had an alert come through when you entered orbit."
texts.zh: 突然，$rank 愣了一下，然后露出了吃惊的表情。"$playerName？那是你，对不对？现役辅助军，对吧？当你进入轨道的时候，触发了一个警报。"

texts.en: "Look, sorry about all of this," $heOrShe indicates the protest. "Tell you what- I can route you and your crew through secure access so you don't have to wait on the circus."
texts.zh: "听着，我对此感到十分抱歉。" $heOrShe表示抗议，"这么和你说吧，我可以把你和你的人送到安全通道，这样你就不必在这马戏场里等着了。"

options.zh: 谢了，但是我会在这等着。

texts.en: The $rank waves a cadet over, giving them instructions to lead you, your guards, and a few of your crew given shore leave - who are looking increasingly impatient - through an alternate route to the commercial promenade.
texts.zh: $rank 挥手招来一名学员，指示他带着你，你的警卫和一些获准上岸的船员 —— 他们看起来越来越不耐烦 —— 从另一条路线前往商业街。

texts.en: The $rank nods, and returns to the comms with more professional focus now; the gendarmerie can't be far off.
texts.zh: $rank 点了点头，带着更加专业和专注的状态回到了通讯中；宪兵应该不远了。

texts.en:
You wait. The crowd grows, and grows less patient - a minority jeers and shouts, a few spacers start throwing trash. The Luddics perform their chant-prayer, calling for an end to the orbital burns, arms locked. From fights breaking out, it is clear that there is much support for the Luddic cause outside of the overt protestors.

It feels near a boiling point when heads start to turn and you see a dark regiment of lightly armored troopers deploy from columns into a wedge. Security drones hum overhead, targeting lasers and ID-cams flickering.
texts.zh:
你冷眼旁观。聚集的人越来越多，也越来越没有耐心 —— 一小部分人发出嘲笑和叫喊，有些宇宙民开始朝人群丢垃圾。卢德教徒们手拉着手，吟唱祷文，呼吁停止使用轨道射线焚烧地表植被。从打斗中可以看出，除了公开的抗议者，还有许多人支持这项运动。

当局势接近失控时，人们突然转头看向一个方向，你发现一支装备轻武器的秘密部队正从方队改为楔形队列。治安无人机在人群头顶上嗡嗡作响，瞄准激光和 ID 扫描仪不停闪烁着。

texts.en:
A steady advance breaks the protest line apart, shock-prods rise and fall to silence shouts and screams. It is difficult to see through the pacification gas, but you can make out drones deploying restraint foam on struggling forms. The Luddics' fists, signs, and even hammers are useless against the power-armored gendarmerie.

"You may pass safely, citizen," a drone buzzes at you in a pleasant voice.

Stepping toward the main promenade, you turn to find that you've left a diminishing trail of blood-spots. A scuff or two of your heel on the deck plate takes care of the problem.
texts.zh:
军队的稳步推进冲散了抗议者的队列，他们挥舞着手中的电击棒，让所有尖叫和呼喊都归于虚无，透过镇暴气体，你可以模糊的辨认出无人机正在释放抑制泡沫来压制挣扎的人。卢德信徒的拳头，标语牌，甚至是铁锤，在装备动力装甲的宪兵面前显得苍白无力。

"你可以安全通过了，公民。" 一架无人机以悦耳的声音对你嗡嗡作响。

当你大步走向主港区时，你转过身来，发现脚上沾满了抗议者的鲜血，在身后留下一排逐渐模糊的血脚印。你用鞋跟在甲板上猛蹭了两下，摆脱了这点不适。

texts.en:
You calmly approach the Luddic protestors, asking to speak to an organizer. They are reluctant to identify a leader who would make an obvious target for MuniSec guards, but soon enough you are recognized by one of the better-dressed Luddics. It appears that your reputation precedes you.

They enthusiastically vouch for you, "a true friend of the Church", and manage to persuade the protestors to clear a path for you and your landing party.

As you step into the commercial promenade, past merchants and spacers annoyed at your special treatment, you begin to hear amplified orders to disperse from the Hegemony gendarmerie.
texts.zh:
你冷静地走向卢德抗议者们，请求与他们的组织者谈一谈。他们虽然冒着被地方安全部重点关注的风险请出了一位领导者，但看起来很不情愿。不过很快，你就被一名衣冠楚楚的卢德信众认出来了 —— 看起来你已经声名远扬。

他们热情地担保你为 "教会真正的朋友"，并且设法说服抗议者们，为你和你的登陆小队让出一条道路。

在你走过那些被你的特殊待遇惹恼的商人和宇宙民，去往商业街的时候，你开始听到 霸主 宪兵那音量放大的驱散命令。

texts.en:
You step forward, proclaiming that you wish to join the protest. At first the Luddics are disbelieving, but as you turn to face the bewildered MuniSec guards and take up the Luddic chant-prayer, a small cheer erupts.

You see $PersonRank $personLastName shake $hisOrHer head in disbelief.
texts.zh:
你迈步向前，宣称你也希望加入抗议。起初，卢德信众并不相信，但随着你转身面对困惑的地方安全部守卫，并开始颂唱卢德祷文，人群中爆发出一阵小小的欢呼。

你看到 $PersonRank $personLastName 难以置信地摇着头。

texts.en: Later, you compare bruises and cuts with your fellow protestors. Your bodyguards, reacting admirably to the unusual situation, managed to shield you from the worst of the gendarmes' beatings, pacification gas, and restraint foam. But you took your hits and have proven yourself to these Luddic pilgrims. You take the opportunity to explain that-
texts.zh: 不久之后，你和你的抗议者同伴们相互打量着身上的淤青和切口。面对这样异乎寻常的情景，你的保镖做出了绝佳的反应，设法将你从宪兵们最毒辣的殴打，镇静气体，以及拘束泡沫中保了下来。不过你还是挨了几下，向这些卢德朝圣者证明了自己。趁此机会，你解释道 ——

options.en: Despite being a non-believer, you support their rights
options.zh: 尽管身为一名无信者，你还是支持他们的权利

options.en: This shared experience brings you all closer to Ludd
options.zh: 共患难的经历令你们离卢德更近了

options.en: In due time, the heretics will pay for these beatings ten-fold
options.zh: 终有一日，要十倍地将这顿毒打奉还给那些异端

options.en: You just wanted to feel what it was like to lose a fight
options.zh: 你只是想尝尝战败的滋味

texts.en:
The pilgrims welcome you as a respectable outsider, pledging hospitality if you visit their homesteads and congregations.

They tell you of the shrine of Jangala, and of being exposed to the toxic xenolife - far more painful, they claim, than anything MuniSec could do to them.

Your name is called from the commsplate.
texts.zh:
朝圣者们欢迎你的到来，认为你是一位可敬的外乡人。他们承诺，如果你来拜访他们的家宅和会众，那你一定会得到殷勤接待。

他们告诉你 Jangala 圣地的事，并讲述着暴露在剧毒异种生命下的体验 —— 他们声称，这种痛苦甚至远胜于地方安全部最酷烈的暴行。

通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en:
It's $rank $personName again, $hisOrHer demeanor cold and martial.

"The rules are simple, captain," $heOrShe says, ice-cold, "And we've been very, very lenient with you. But there seems to be a failure to communicate, so let me explain in very small words how it works around here."

A guard sets a plastic tray of your personal belongings on the battered table of the processing room. The Hegemony $rank continues, slowly; each word given emphasis. "Pay your tariffs. Don't disrupt business."

$HeOrShe turns and motions at some guards, "Now get out of my sight."
texts.zh:
来者又是 $personName $rank，举止冷峻，金戈铁马。

"规矩很简单，舰长。" $HeOrShe语气冰冷，"我们对你已经极其，极其的宽容了。然而，看起来交涉还是失败了，那我就用最简短的话来把这儿的规矩说清楚。"

一名警卫把装着你个人物品的塑料托盘放在审讯室那破旧的桌子上。与此同时，这名 霸主 $rank 逐字逐句地继续说道："付关税，别碍事。"

$HeOrShe转过身对警卫打了个手势，"现在，你可以滚了。"

texts.en:
You are shoved, squinting, into the bright light of the plaza outside of the municipal security processing center.

Dignity largely unbruised, you secure your sidearm (cellmag confiscated), run a quick check on your personal datapad, and give a nod to your second officer - who has been waiting patiently with two hot drinks.
texts.zh:
你被推到市政安全审核中心外面的广场上，明亮的光芒使你不由得眯起眼睛。

你的尊严被很大程度的保留了，你保护好自己的随身武器 (弹匣已没收)，快速检查了自己的私人数据平板，然后对你的二副点了点头 —— 他带着两杯热饮，一直耐心地等着你。

texts.en:
The pilgrims welcome you as one of their own, pledging their hospitality if you visit their homesteads, and promising a seat for you at the front of their congregation's service to welcome returning pilgrims.

They tell you of the shrine of Jangala, and of being exposed to the toxic xenolife - far more painful, they claim, than anything MuniSec can do to them.

Your name is called from the commsplate.
texts.zh:
朝圣者们像欢迎同道那样欢迎你。他们承诺，如果你来拜访他们的家宅和会众，那你一定会得到殷勤接待，并且保证给你在他们会众服务站的前排留一个座位，以便欢迎那些归来的朝圣者。

他们告诉你 Jangala 圣地的事，并讲述着暴露在剧毒异种生命下的体验 —— 他们声称，这种痛苦甚至远胜于地方安全部最酷烈的暴行。

通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en:
Most of the protestors are alarmed by your rhetoric, glancing nervously toward unseen observation devices and drawing away from your corner of the holding cell. Though a couple younger pilgrims and one much older, with scars to show his commitment, remain near you, eyes daring the others to speak their criticism aloud.

"We hear you, $playerBrotherOrSister. The end of the Path is near," he whispers, and tells you of the Jangala Shrine, of mortification of the flesh through exposure to the xenolife - worse than anything MuniSec could hope to inflict.

Your name is called from the commsplate.
texts.zh:
大多数抗议者被你的激进言论吓到，紧张的瞥了一眼不可视的监视装置，抽身离开了属于你的牢房角落。尽管几个年轻的朝圣者和一位老者 —— 他身上的伤痕记述着他的奉献 —— 留在你身旁，目光盯着其他人，大声批判着。

"我们听说过你，$playerBrotherOrSister，卢德之道的终点已经近在咫尺。" 他轻声耳语，对你讲述着 Jangala 圣地的事，讲述着暴露在异种生命中对肉身所造成的折辱 —— 远远超过地方安全部的任何打压手段。

通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en: The Luddic protestors are confused and even a little alarmed by your explanation - it seems they've been locked in with a crazy person. They physically draw away from your corner of the holding cell until your name is called through the commsplate.
texts.zh: 这些卢德抗议者们对你的解释感到困惑，甚至有点害怕 —— 看起来他们和一个狂人关在一起了。他们挪动身体离开了属于你的牢房角落，直到通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en: The $faction $rank shakes $hisOrHer head. "Appreciate the patriotic gesture, citizen, but we'll handle this. Got to be delicate," $heOrShe says with annoyance, "It's very... political."
texts.zh: $faction $rank摇了摇$hisOrHer的头。"感谢你的爱国情怀，公民，但我们会处理这件事，这事一定要谨慎，" $heOrShe恼怒地说，"这件事...非常有政治影响。"

texts.en: Suddenly the $rank does a double-take. "$playerName? That's you, isn't it? Commissioned Auxiliary, right? Had an alert come through when you entered orbit."
texts.zh: 突然，$rank 愣了一下，然后露出了吃惊的表情。"$playerName？那是你，对不对？现役辅助军，对吧？当你进入轨道的时候，触发了一个警报。"

texts.en:
$HeOrShe seems to think it over for a second, then glances at a small datapad.

"Tell you what; get your marines here in three minutes and subsume to my command, here's the comm-code. I want min-force, zero fire and flash; weapons locked to my authorization."
texts.zh:
$HeOrShe想了一小会，然后看向了一个小数据平板。

"给我听好了；让你的陆战队员在三分钟之内过来，一切听我的指挥，这是通讯代码。我要以最低限度的武力来镇压叛乱，任何会发光和喷火的玩意都不要；武器必须在我的授权下才准许使用。"

options.en: On second thought, I'll let you handle this.
options.zh: 仔细想想，我还是让你来处理吧。

texts.en:
You coordinate a joint response, a squad of your marines able to quickly deploy on the dock-side and coordinate with the Hegemony gendarmerie on the opposite end of the protest. A steady advance breaks the protest line apart with minimal use of force - the Luddics' fists, hammers, and signs useless against power-armored troops.

$Rank $personName is busy coordinating arrests in the aftermath but manages to catch your eye and give a quick half-salute as you leave toward the commercial promenade.
texts.zh:
你组织了一次联合行动，你的陆战队员迅速部署在码头侧面，和位于抗议者们另一头的 霸主 宪兵展开配合。你们的部队稳步推进，以最低限度的武力镇压了抗议队伍 —— 卢德信众的拳头，铁锤，以及标语牌，面对动力装甲部队显得苍白无力。

$Rank $personName 忙着组织事后的逮捕行动，但当你离开此地去往商业街的时候，他还是在百忙中对你示意，快速地向你敬了一个半礼。

texts.en: The $rank nods, distractedly. "As you will, captain."
texts.zh: $rank 心烦意乱地点了点头，"如你所愿，舰长。"

texts.en:
You order a small squad of your own marines, armaments and munitions removed due to port regulations, on a fast shuttle from your $shipOrFleet.

The marines, in full power armor, form a vanguard before you and simply march into the protesting Luddics.
texts.zh:
你从自己的陆战队里要来一支小队，坐着穿梭机从你的$shipOrFleet高速赶来。鉴于港口规定，没有携带武器弹药。

这些陆战队员身着全套动力装甲，在你身前组成一支先锋，仅仅是简单地朝着抗议的卢德信众展开行军，没有其他多余的举动。

texts.en:
The protestors' line is easily broken by your armored marines, as are not a few limbs. The MuniSec guards manage to exploit the situation and corral the protesters - now crying, screaming, and shouting abuse at you in particular - into ineffective huddles.

The Hegemony officer overseeing the official response looks not simply annoyed, but livid.
texts.zh:
抗议者的队列被你全副武装的陆战队员轻而易举地尽数冲散。地方安全部的守卫们趁势出手，迫使这些抗议者们 —— 他们现在哭喊，尖叫着，甚至对你破口大骂 —— 无能为力地缩成一团。

负责监督官方回应的 霸主 官员看起来对你的意见不小，已经脸色发青了。

texts.en:
"I should have you arrested!" $heOrShe shouts, then, ignoring your armored marines - who dare not touch a Hegemony officer on their own station - gets close to your face, "Your little stunt just gave them a propaganda holo that'll recruit hundreds of Pather terrorists," $heOrShe seethes.

"Get your goons out of my sight before I call in the real marines."
texts.zh:
"我真应该逮捕你！" $heOrShe怒吼着赶到你的面前，无视了你那些全副武装的陆战队员 —— 他们也不敢在 霸主 的地盘上对军官撒野，"你愚蠢的行为会被拍进全息图里，而这会带来几百名左径分子，" $heOrShe咬牙切齿地说。

"在我集结真正的军队之前，让你的暴徒滚出我的视线。"
effects: MarketCMD addUnrest jangala 3 "Strikes and protests due to vigilante anti-Luddic violence"

texts.en: As you step onto the commercial promenade you see both crew and locals pointing and staring. Some hold datapad, recording holos...
texts.zh: 当你走进商业街时，你看到船员和当地居民对着什么东西指手画脚。一些人还拿着数据平板和有记录功能的全息影像设备。

texts.en:
The concourse is in chaos. A crowd of protestors in Luddic greens has formed a human barrier across the main entrance. Surrounding them are angry spacers, officers and crew alike, waiting to enter the commercial promenade or return to their ships.

A small contingent of local MuniSec holds the shouting crowds apart - barely.
texts.zh:
港区陷入了一片混乱，一群身着卢德绿袍的抗议者在主要出入口形成了人墙。周遭堵满了想要进入商业街或返回舰船的宇宙民、军官与船员，他们现在怒气冲天。

一支地方安全部的小分队勉强把喧闹的人群隔开。

texts.en:
You recognize the Hegemony $post, $name speaking orders into a small comms unit. $HeOrShe notices you, and nods you over.

"Luddics protesting the planet-side burns," $heOrShe explains. "Get these every other week due to the pilgrims. They consider it a sort of rite of passage."

$HeOrShe one-arm shrugs to suggest that $heOrShe doesn't find the matter worth getting too upset over, then speaks another string of tactical jargon into $hisOrHer comms.
texts.zh:
你认出了那个霸主 $post，$name 正通过一个小型通讯器下达着命令。$HeOrShe注意到了你，并向你点头示意。

"卢德教徒正在抗议轨道焚化。" $HeOrShe解释说，"由于朝圣者的原因，这种事情每隔一周就会发生一次。他们都把这当成朝圣之路上的某种仪式了。"

$HeOrShe耸了耸半边肩膀，一副这事也不值得让$HeOrShe太上心的样子。随后$hisOrHer对着通讯器又说了一串战术术语。

texts.en:
You wait. The crowd grows, and grows less patient - a minority jeers and shouts, a few spacers start throwing trash. The Luddics perform their chant-prayer, calling for an end to the orbital burns, arms locked. From fights breaking out, it is clear that there is much support for the Luddic cause outside of the overt protestors.

It feels near a boiling point when heads start to turn and you see a dark regiment of lightly armored troopers deploy from columns into a wedge. Security drones hum overhead, targeting lasers and ID-cams flickering.
texts.zh:
你冷眼旁观。聚集的人越来越多，也越来越没有耐心 —— 一小部分人发出嘲笑和叫喊，有些宇宙民开始朝人群丢垃圾。卢德教徒们手拉着手，吟唱祷文，呼吁停止使用轨道射线焚烧地表植被。从打斗中可以看出，除了公开的抗议者，还有许多人支持这项运动。

当局势接近失控时，人们突然转头看向一个方向，你发现一支装备轻武器的秘密部队正从方队改为楔形队列。治安无人机在人群头顶上嗡嗡作响，瞄准激光和 ID 扫描仪不停闪烁着。

texts.en:
A steady advance breaks the protest line apart, shock-prods rise and fall to silence shouts and screams. It is difficult to see through the pacification gas, but you can make out drones deploying restraint foam on struggling forms. The Luddics' fists, signs, and even hammers are useless against the power-armored gendarmerie.

"You may pass safely, citizen," a drone buzzes at you in a pleasant voice.

Stepping toward the main promenade, you turn to find that you've left a diminishing trail of blood-spots. A scuff or two of your heel on the deck plate takes care of the problem.
texts.zh:
军队的稳步推进冲散了抗议者的队列，他们挥舞着手中的电击棒，让所有尖叫和呼喊都归于虚无，透过镇暴气体，你可以模糊的辨认出无人机正在释放抑制泡沫来压制挣扎的人。卢德信徒的拳头，标语牌，甚至是铁锤，在装备动力装甲的宪兵面前显得苍白无力。

"你可以安全通过了，公民。" 一架无人机以悦耳的声音对你嗡嗡作响。

当你大步走向主港区时，你转过身来，发现脚上沾满了抗议者的鲜血，在身后留下一排逐渐模糊的血脚印。你用鞋跟在甲板上猛蹭了两下，摆脱了这点不适。

texts.en: The $faction $rank shakes $hisOrHer head. "Appreciate the patriotic gesture, citizen, but we'll handle this. Got to be delicate," $heOrShe says with annoyance, "It's very... political."
texts.zh: $faction $rank摇了摇$hisOrHer的头。"感谢你的爱国情怀，公民，但我们会处理这件事，这事一定要谨慎，" $heOrShe恼怒地说，"这件事...非常有政治影响。"

texts.en: Suddenly the $rank does a double-take. "$playerName? That's you, isn't it? Commissioned Auxiliary, right? Had an alert come through when you entered orbit."
texts.zh: 突然，$rank 愣了一下，然后露出了吃惊的表情。"$playerName？那是你，对不对？现役辅助军，对吧？当你进入轨道的时候，触发了一个警报。"

texts.en:
$HeOrShe seems to think it over for a second, then glances at a small datapad.

"Tell you what; get your marines here in three minutes and subsume to my command, here's the comm-code. I want min-force, zero fire and flash; weapons locked to my authorization."
texts.zh:
$HeOrShe想了一小会，然后看向了一个小数据平板。

"给我听好了；让你的陆战队员在三分钟之内过来，一切听我的指挥，这是通讯代码。我要以最低限度的武力来镇压叛乱，任何会发光和喷火的玩意都不要；武器必须在我的授权下才准许使用。"

options.en: On second thought, I'll let you handle this.
options.zh: 仔细想想，我还是让你来处理吧。

texts.en:
You coordinate a joint response, a squad of your marines able to quickly deploy on the dock-side and coordinate with the Hegemony gendarmerie on the opposite end of the protest. A steady advance breaks the protest line apart with minimal use of force - the Luddics' fists, hammers, and signs useless against power-armored troops.

$Rank $personName is busy coordinating arrests in the aftermath but manages to catch your eye and give a quick half-salute as you leave toward the commercial promenade.
texts.zh:
你组织了一次联合行动，你的陆战队员迅速部署在码头侧面，和位于抗议者们另一头的 霸主 宪兵展开配合。你们的部队稳步推进，以最低限度的武力镇压了抗议队伍 —— 卢德信众的拳头，铁锤，以及标语牌，面对动力装甲部队显得苍白无力。

$Rank $personName 忙着组织事后的逮捕行动，但当你离开此地去往商业街的时候，他还是在百忙中对你示意，快速地向你敬了一个半礼。

texts.en: The $rank nods, distractedly. "As you will, captain."
texts.zh: $rank 心烦意乱地点了点头，"如你所愿，舰长。"

texts.en:
"Not here," $heOrShe says, eyes not leaving the protestors. "On the surface. For appreciating the local plant-life. Don't understand why, you wouldn't believe how toxic the stuff is. Detox after exposure is like a week of hangover compressed down into a day or two."

$HeOrShe shakes $hisOrHer head. "At least that's what it felt like for me. Guess they like suffering. Luddics for you. Top brass says we gotta humor 'em. Politics, right?"

A burst of coded garble comes through the comms, and the $post gives a short response. "Gendarmerie will be here soon if you want to stay for the show," $heOrShe says.
texts.zh:
"有，不过不在这里，" $heOrShe说，视线并没有离开抗议者，"是在地表上，朝圣者们喜欢在那欣赏当地的植物。我不理解。你想象不到那些玩意的毒性有多强。人体暴露在那种环境中后，后续的排毒过程十分痛苦，好比是把整整一周的宿醉压缩到一至两天。"

$HeOrShe摇了摇头。"反正我的亲身体验就是这样的。可能这帮人就是喜欢受苦吧。这就是卢德信徒。上面的人说我们必须迁就他们。这就是政治，对吧？"

通讯器中传来一阵噪声，$post给出了一个简短的回答。"如果你想看看接下来会发生什么，宪兵马上就到了。" $heOrShe说。

texts.en: Suddenly the $rank does a double-take. "$playerName? That's you, isn't it? Commissioned Auxiliary, right? Had an alert come through when you entered orbit."
texts.zh: 突然，$rank 愣了一下，然后露出了吃惊的表情。"$playerName？那是你，对不对？现役辅助军，对吧？当你进入轨道的时候，触发了一个警报。"

texts.en: Suddenly the $rank does a double-take. "$playerName? That's you, isn't it? Commissioned Auxiliary, right? Had an alert come through when you entered orbit."
texts.zh: 突然，$rank 愣了一下，然后露出了吃惊的表情。"$playerName？那是你，对不对？现役辅助军，对吧？当你进入轨道的时候，触发了一个警报。"

texts.en: "Look, sorry about all of this," $heOrShe indicates the protest. "Tell you what- I can route you and your crew through secure access so you don't have to wait on the circus."
texts.zh: "听着，我对此感到十分抱歉。" $heOrShe表示抗议，"这么和你说吧，我可以把你和你的人送到安全通道，这样你就不必在这马戏场里等着了。"

options.zh: 谢了，但是我会在这等着。

texts.en: The $rank nods, and returns to the comms with more professional focus now; the gendarmerie can't be far off.
texts.zh: $rank 点了点头，带着更加专业和专注的状态回到了通讯中；宪兵应该不远了。

texts.en: The $rank waves a cadet over, giving them instructions to lead you, your guards, and a few of your crew given shore leave - who are looking increasingly impatient - through an alternate route to the commercial promenade.
texts.zh: $rank 挥手招来一名学员，指示他带着你，你的警卫和一些获准上岸的船员 —— 他们看起来越来越不耐烦 —— 从另一条路线前往商业街。

texts.en:
You calmly approach the Luddic protestors, asking to speak to an organizer. They are reluctant to identify a leader who would make an obvious target for MuniSec guards, but soon enough you are recognized by one of the better-dressed Luddics. It appears that your reputation precedes you.

They enthusiastically vouch for you, "a true friend of the Church", and manage to persuade the protestors to clear a path for you and your landing party.

As you step into the commercial promenade, past merchants and spacers annoyed at your special treatment, you begin to hear amplified orders to disperse from the Hegemony gendarmerie.
texts.zh:
你冷静地走向卢德抗议者们，请求与他们的组织者谈一谈。他们虽然冒着被地方安全部重点关注的风险请出了一位领导者，但看起来很不情愿。不过很快，你就被一名衣冠楚楚的卢德信众认出来了 —— 看起来你已经声名远扬。

他们热情地担保你为 "教会真正的朋友"，并且设法说服抗议者们，为你和你的登陆小队让出一条道路。

在你走过那些被你的特殊待遇惹恼的商人和宇宙民，去往商业街的时候，你开始听到 霸主 宪兵那音量放大的驱散命令。

texts.en:
You step forward, proclaiming that you wish to join the protest. At first the Luddics are disbelieving, but as you turn to face the bewildered MuniSec guards and take up the Luddic chant-prayer, a small cheer erupts.

You see $PersonRank $personLastName shake $hisOrHer head in disbelief.
texts.zh:
你迈步向前，宣称你也希望加入抗议。起初，卢德信众并不相信，但随着你转身面对困惑的地方安全部守卫，并开始颂唱卢德祷文，人群中爆发出一阵小小的欢呼。

你看到 $PersonRank $personLastName 难以置信地摇着头。

texts.en: Later, you compare bruises and cuts with your fellow protestors. Your bodyguards, reacting admirably to the unusual situation, managed to shield you from the worst of the gendarmes' beatings, pacification gas, and restraint foam. But you took your hits and have proven yourself to these Luddic pilgrims. You take the opportunity to explain that-
texts.zh: 不久之后，你和你的抗议者同伴们相互打量着身上的淤青和切口。面对这样异乎寻常的情景，你的保镖做出了绝佳的反应，设法将你从宪兵们最毒辣的殴打，镇静气体，以及拘束泡沫中保了下来。不过你还是挨了几下，向这些卢德朝圣者证明了自己。趁此机会，你解释道 ——

options.en: Despite being a non-believer, you support their rights
options.zh: 尽管身为一名无信者，你还是支持他们的权利

options.en: This shared experience brings you all closer to Ludd
options.zh: 共患难的经历令你们离卢德更近了

options.en: In due time, the heretics will pay for these beatings ten-fold
options.zh: 终有一日，要十倍地将这顿毒打奉还给那些异端

options.en: You just wanted to feel what it was like to lose a fight
options.zh: 你只是想尝尝战败的滋味

texts.en:
The pilgrims welcome you as a respectable outsider, pledging hospitality if you visit their homesteads and congregations.

They tell you of the shrine of Jangala, and of being exposed to the toxic xenolife - far more painful, they claim, than anything MuniSec could do to them.

Your name is called from the commsplate.
texts.zh:
朝圣者们欢迎你的到来，认为你是一位可敬的外乡人。他们承诺，如果你来拜访他们的家宅和会众，那你一定会得到殷勤接待。

他们告诉你 Jangala 圣地的事，并讲述着暴露在剧毒异种生命下的体验 —— 他们声称，这种痛苦甚至远胜于地方安全部最酷烈的暴行。

通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en:
The pilgrims welcome you as one of their own, pledging their hospitality if you visit their homesteads, and promising a seat for you at the front of their congregation's service to welcome returning pilgrims.

They tell you of the shrine of Jangala, and of being exposed to the toxic xenolife - far more painful, they claim, than anything MuniSec can do to them.

Your name is called from the commsplate.
texts.zh:
朝圣者们像欢迎同道那样欢迎你。他们承诺，如果你来拜访他们的家宅和会众，那你一定会得到殷勤接待，并且保证给你在他们会众服务站的前排留一个座位，以便欢迎那些归来的朝圣者。

他们告诉你 Jangala 圣地的事，并讲述着暴露在剧毒异种生命下的体验 —— 他们声称，这种痛苦甚至远胜于地方安全部最酷烈的暴行。

通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en:
Most of the protestors are alarmed by your rhetoric, glancing nervously toward unseen observation devices and drawing away from your corner of the holding cell. Though a couple younger pilgrims and one much older, with scars to show his commitment, remain near you, eyes daring the others to speak their criticism aloud.

"We hear you, $playerBrotherOrSister. The end of the Path is near," he whispers, and tells you of the Jangala Shrine, of mortification of the flesh through exposure to the xenolife - worse than anything MuniSec could hope to inflict.

Your name is called from the commsplate.
texts.zh:
大多数抗议者被你的激进言论吓到，紧张的瞥了一眼不可视的监视装置，抽身离开了属于你的牢房角落。尽管几个年轻的朝圣者和一位老者 —— 他身上的伤痕记述着他的奉献 —— 留在你身旁，目光盯着其他人，大声批判着。

"我们听说过你，$playerBrotherOrSister，卢德之道的终点已经近在咫尺。" 他轻声耳语，对你讲述着 Jangala 圣地的事，讲述着暴露在异种生命中对肉身所造成的折辱 —— 远远超过地方安全部的任何打压手段。

通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en: The Luddic protestors are confused and even a little alarmed by your explanation - it seems they've been locked in with a crazy person. They physically draw away from your corner of the holding cell until your name is called through the commsplate.
texts.zh: 这些卢德抗议者们对你的解释感到困惑，甚至有点害怕 —— 看起来他们和一个狂人关在一起了。他们挪动身体离开了属于你的牢房角落，直到通信板呼叫了你的名字。

texts.en:
It's $rank $personName again, $hisOrHer demeanor cold and martial.

"The rules are simple, captain," $heOrShe says, ice-cold, "And we've been very, very lenient with you. But there seems to be a failure to communicate, so let me explain in very small words how it works around here."

A guard sets a plastic tray of your personal belongings on the battered table of the processing room. The Hegemony $rank continues, slowly; each word given emphasis. "Pay your tariffs. Don't disrupt business."

$HeOrShe turns and motions at some guards, "Now get out of my sight."
texts.zh:
来者又是 $personName $rank，举止冷峻，金戈铁马。

"规矩很简单，舰长。" $HeOrShe语气冰冷，"我们对你已经极其，极其的宽容了。然而，看起来交涉还是失败了，那我就用最简短的话来把这儿的规矩说清楚。"

一名警卫把装着你个人物品的塑料托盘放在审讯室那破旧的桌子上。与此同时，这名 霸主 $rank 逐字逐句地继续说道："付关税，别碍事。"

$HeOrShe转过身对警卫打了个手势，"现在，你可以滚了。"

texts.en:
You are shoved, squinting, into the bright light of the plaza outside of the municipal security processing center.

Dignity largely unbruised, you secure your sidearm (cellmag confiscated), run a quick check on your personal datapad, and give a nod to your second officer - who has been waiting patiently with two hot drinks.
texts.zh:
你被推到市政安全审核中心外面的广场上，明亮的光芒使你不由得眯起眼睛。

你的尊严被很大程度的保留了，你保护好自己的随身武器 (弹匣已没收)，快速检查了自己的私人数据平板，然后对你的二副点了点头 —— 他带着两杯热饮，一直耐心地等着你。

texts.en:
You order a small squad of your own marines, armaments and munitions removed due to port regulations, on a fast shuttle from your $shipOrFleet.

The marines, in full power armor, form a vanguard before you and simply march into the protesting Luddics.
texts.zh:
你从自己的陆战队里要来一支小队，坐着穿梭机从你的$shipOrFleet高速赶来。鉴于港口规定，没有携带武器弹药。

这些陆战队员身着全套动力装甲，在你身前组成一支先锋，仅仅是简单地朝着抗议的卢德信众展开行军，没有其他多余的举动。

texts.en:
The protestors' line is easily broken by your armored marines, as are not a few limbs. The MuniSec guards manage to exploit the situation and corral the protesters - now crying, screaming, and shouting abuse at you in particular - into ineffective huddles.

The Hegemony officer overseeing the official response looks not simply annoyed, but livid.
texts.zh:
抗议者的队列被你全副武装的陆战队员轻而易举地尽数冲散。地方安全部的守卫们趁势出手，迫使这些抗议者们 —— 他们现在哭喊，尖叫着，甚至对你破口大骂 —— 无能为力地缩成一团。

负责监督官方回应的 霸主 官员看起来对你的意见不小，已经脸色发青了。

texts.en:
"I should have you arrested!" $heOrShe shouts, then, ignoring your armored marines - who dare not touch a Hegemony officer on their own station - gets close to your face, "Your little stunt just gave them a propaganda holo that'll recruit hundreds of Pather terrorists," $heOrShe seethes.

"Get your goons out of my sight before I call in the real marines."
texts.zh:
"我真应该逮捕你！" $heOrShe怒吼着赶到你的面前，无视了你那些全副武装的陆战队员 —— 他们也不敢在 霸主 的地盘上对军官撒野，"你愚蠢的行为会被拍进全息图里，而这会带来几百名左径分子，" $heOrShe咬牙切齿地说。

"在我集结真正的军队之前，让你的暴徒滚出我的视线。"
effects: MarketCMD addUnrest jangala 3 "Strikes and protests due to vigilante anti-Luddic violence"

texts.en: As you step onto the commercial promenade you see both crew and locals pointing and staring. Some hold datapad, recording holos...
texts.zh: 当你走进商业街时，你看到船员和当地居民对着什么东西指手画脚。一些人还拿着数据平板和有记录功能的全息影像设备。

options.en: Take a shuttle to visit the Luddic shrine
options.zh: 乘坐穿梭机前去拜访卢德圣地

texts.en:
Your shuttle descends toward verdant continents crowned by lethargically churning storm systems. The orbital burn lasers flicker from the spark of Jangala station, invisible until they cut lines of plasma through the atmosphere.

You pass through blinding cloud cover, the light taking on a sickly hue of green. Your viewport is streaked with marching droplets of spore-laden water as the shuttle slows to drop softly onto the landing pad nearly lost in the overgrowth of Jangalan foliage.
texts.zh:
你的穿梭机降落在苍翠的陆地上，翻腾的风暴在地表缓慢移动着。伴随着 Jangala 空间站上闪烁的光斑，轨道激光倾泻而下，在大气层中切出耀眼的等离子火焰。

你穿过炫目的云层，映入眼帘的是一片令人头晕的绿色。舷窗外，饱含孢子的雨滴如行军般奔流而下；穿梭机减速缓降，轻柔地停靠在几乎被 Jangala 疯长的植被彻底吞没的停机坪上。

texts.en:
The verdant continents of Jangala sprawl beneath you, crowned by huge weather systems churning lethargic and magisterial.

Searing lines of orbital burn lasers flick out from Jangala station, invisible until they cut slashes of plasma through the thick atmosphere. Burn-glow competes with rampaging electrical storms to illuminate the mountainous cloud formations from below.
texts.zh:
Jangala 青翠的大陆在你脚下延伸，巨型的云层在你的头顶上慵懒地翻腾着。

炽热的轨道激光从 Jangala 空间站中喷涌而出，在大气层中划出一道道炫目的等离子体。燃烧的辉光和云层中的闪电交相辉映，照亮了下面那些如山峦般厚重的云层。

texts.en:
The reception lounge is filled with parties of Luddic pilgrims in traditional handweave led by subcurates in ritual hand-washing. A glance upward reveals the true cleansing: a battery of air-purification units caught in a tangle of murmuring ducts.

Foliage presses itself almost sensually against the outer viewports, letting in only dim light. The plant life seems to twitch, liquids oozing over the panes from cracks in bladders and tubules, leaving rivulets cutting across flaking encrustations. Between the zeal of the foliage and hand-crafted charm of Luddic engineering, the place feels distinctly worrisome compared to the environmental containment you are accustomed to.
texts.zh:
接待休息室里挤满了在此聚会的卢德朝圣者。他们身着传统的手工服装，由助理祭司带领进行仪式性的净手。向上看一眼，你就会发现这里真正的清洁设施：淹没在复杂管道中的一组空气净化装置。

舞动着的叶片几乎堵死了窗户，只有些许昏暗的光线照射进来。这些富有生机的植物似乎在抽搐着，液体从囊状器官和小管的裂缝中渗出，留下一条条涓涓细流划过剥落的外壳。在植物的躁动和卢德工艺的魅力之间，与你习惯的，那些被精心调控的环境相比，这个地方明显令人担忧。

texts.en:
One of the shrine's attendants instantly recognizes that you're not one of the usual pilgrims and intercepts you, making remarkable speed despite wearing awkward-looking novice's robes.

The attendant smiles piously, hands held together. "How might we assist you?"
texts.zh:
圣地的一名圣务侍立即意识到你不是寻常的朝圣者。尽管穿着看起来很尴尬的新手长袍，他还是很快地拦住了你。

圣务侍双手合十，虔诚地微笑着。"我们能为您提供什么帮助？"

texts.en:
One of the shrine's attendants scurries to meet you.

"The complex is kept overpressurized," they say, following your gaze, "so if there were a breach, there would be plenty of time to find and seal the leak."

The attendant creates what must be intended to be a reassuring smile. "How might we assist you?"
texts.zh:
圣地的圣务侍赶忙出来迎接你。

"这片建筑群一直处于超载状态，" 跟随着你的目光，他们说道，"所以，如果哪里有漏洞，我们应该能有足够的时间发现并将其密封。"

圣务侍做出一个令人安心的笑容。"我们能为您提供什么帮助？"

options.en: I'd like to visit the shrine.
I wish to visit the shrine. Outside.
options.zh: 我希望参拜圣地。在户外。

texts.en:
You are led past heavy curtains which mute the murmur of pilgrims and shut out all artificial light. Pilgrims kneel in the shrine-chamber, silhouetted before the glowing panes to without lit by that sickly yellow-green cloud cover.

Beyond, you see the statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting fruiting bodies of xenolife. Among them are pilgrims, exposed in only light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth. At their feet, covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium or alien equivalents, are bones. Or are they fallen branches, overgrown rocks? The final wish for terminally-devoted fanatics, or your imagination?

The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of the minutes you watch, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh:
你被带领着穿过厚重的幕布，这些布料阻隔了朝圣者的低语，挡住了所有的人造光源。朝圣者们跪倒在神殿内，他们在明亮的窗格前被勾勒出轮廓，不必被那病态的黄绿色云层照亮。

在远处，你看到了那座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了异种生命的子实体。只穿着浅色长袍的朝圣者夹杂其中，疯长的植物轻易淹没了他们。在他们脚下，那被苔藓和菌丝或类似外星生物组成的被子覆盖着的是人骨，还是倒下的树枝和杂乱的岩石？是绝境中狂热信徒的最后愿望，又或者仅仅是你的想象？

在你停留的几分钟里，绿色在不知不觉中汹涌澎湃，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

texts.en: You make your way toward the landing pads, past pilgrims queuing for the charity cafeteria, regrouping before or after visiting the shrine, and otherwise stowing their humble possessions.
texts.zh: 你朝着停机坪走去，路过在慈善食堂前排队的朝圣者。他们或在参拜圣地前后重新聚集，又或者在收起他们微不足道的财物。

texts.en:
The air hits you, warm and wet, like high-G shock foam. You step out and follow the short trail; it seems nearly overgrown. You follow it, leaves and feelers brushing against you.

You find the statue gardens, the forms blistering with growth, crawling with tendrils, sprouting fruiting bodies of xenolife. Among them are pilgrims, exposed in their light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth. How long does it take- hours, days?

At their feet, covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium or alien equivalents, are bones. Or fallen branches, overgrown rocks. Or the final wish for terminally-devoted fanatics.

The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of your stay, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh:
空气刺痛着你，带来温暖又潮湿的感觉，就像高重力缓冲泡沫一样。你沿着小路走了出去，这条路几乎被植物淹没了。你顺着路继续前行，树叶和触须拂过你的身体。

你发现了一座雕像花园，这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了异种生命的子实体。穿着浅色长袍的朝圣者夹杂其中，疯长的植物轻易淹没了他们。形成这一切花费了多少时间？是几个小时，还是数天？

他们的脚下，那被苔藓和菌丝或类似外星生物组成的被子覆盖着的，是骨头，还是枯枝，乱石？是狂热信徒的遗愿，或者只是你自己的想象？

在你停留的几分钟里，绿色在不知不觉中汹涌澎湃，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

options.en: Return to the interior of the complex

texts.en: You undergo a routine decontamination in a stained yet clean chamber built for that purpose. After an oddly-smelling shower, the flicker of lasers, and another round of antixenols, you are given back your clothing. Everything is abrasively dry and smells of disinfectant.
texts.zh: 你在一间整洁但略有污渍的洁净室里接受了例行去污。穿过气味奇怪的淋浴、照过几次激光、又服用了另一轮抗异种感染药物之后，你拿回了你的衣服。所有东西都被强力烘干过，还带着点消毒液的味道。

texts.en: Breathing feels strange, still. You have to think about each breath, filling your lungs, then emptying them.
texts.zh: 呼吸的感觉仍然很奇怪。你不得不仔细进行每一次呼吸，用空气填满你的肺，然后排空它们。

options.en: This seems like a... difficult place to maintain a shrine.
options.zh: 这个地方似乎...很难被维持为一座圣地。

options.en: This seems like a terrible place to put a shrine.
options.zh: 这里看起来不像是个建圣地的好地方。

texts.en:
"Yes, of course. I can show you to the washing station where we ask that all, pilgrim or no, partake of a simple cleansing before visiting the interior shrine."

The attendant starts to shuffle you along into a group of devotees.
texts.zh:
"是，当然可以。我可以带你去净化站，在那里我们要求所有人，无论朝圣者与否，在参观圣地内部之前进行简单的清洁。"

圣务侍把你带进虔信者的队伍中。

options.en: I mean the outside. The real shrine.
options.zh: 我的意思是去外面，去真正的圣地。

texts.en:
You are led past heavy curtains. The murmur of pilgrims is muted, and all artificial light shut out.

Your eyes adjust to the shrine-chamber, taking in rows of silhouetted pilgrims kneeling before polished panes of diamond-matrix, illuminated by the sickly yellow-green cloud cover from without.

Beyond the windows, you see overgrown human figures - a statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting the fruiting bodies of alien life. One moves; not the wind, but another pilgrim, exposed and outdoors. There are people out there, you realize with a start, wearing only light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth.
texts.zh:
你被带领着穿过厚重的幕布。朝圣者的窃窃私语沉寂了下来，所有的人造光源都被熄灭了。

你刚适应神殿内的昏暗光线，就看到一排排的朝圣者跪倒在金刚石方窗前。它们的侧影被外面病态的黄绿色云层所照亮。

在窗外，你看到被植物寄生的人形 —— 那是一座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了外星生命的子实体。其中一个人形移动着 —— 那不是风在吹动，而是另一个在户外的朝圣者。你猛然意识到，外面的人只穿着浅色长袍，这使得他们很容易隐蔽在植物群中。

texts.en:
At their feet, more forms come into focus; covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium, or whatever alien equivalent, which obscures the feet of the statues. Bones. Or are they fallen branches and overgrown rocks? The final wish for some terminally-devoted fanatics, or your imagination set loose?

The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of the minutes you watch, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh:
在他们脚下，更多种类的植物映入眼帘；苔藓和菌丝，或者其他类似的东西，覆盖着雕像的脚。那是人骨，还是倒下的树枝和杂草丛生的岩石？这是一些狂热者的终极渴望，又或者仅仅是你的想象？

在你观察的几分钟里，你并不难察觉到那些搅动着的绿色，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

texts.en:
The attendant looks you over skeptically.

"You are sure of this? You desire this with full knowledge of what exposure to Jangala entails?"

The attendant brings your attention to a row of pamphlets in a tasteful wooden stand displaying what, at a glance, appear to be a selection of truly unholy skin conditions.
texts.zh:
圣务侍一脸疑惑地看着你。

"你认真的？你真的了解暴露在 Jangala 的地表会造成什么后果吗？"

圣务侍示意你留意一旁的雅致木架，上面展示了一排翻开了的宣传册。你瞥了一眼，看来里面应该是精选了各种非常不神圣的皮肤感染症状。

texts.en:
"Would it not be 'foolish', captain, to expose yourself to the outside?" the attendant says, somehow keeping peevishness out of their tone if not words.

As if on cue - or perhaps because they were hovering nearby the whole time - a curate (you presume) of the shrine steps up to you and the attendant, robes not quite resplendent but conveying a sense of care and craft that belies a higher status in the Church.
texts.zh:
"把自己暴露在外面不是很 '愚蠢' 吗，舰长？" 圣务侍说。不知为何，他的语气并不焦躁。

就好像是在暗示，或者可能是因为他们一直在附近徘徊，一位圣地的祭司 (你推测) 走到你和圣务侍面前。他的长袍并不那么华丽，但传达了一种谨慎和诡秘的感觉，这掩盖了他们在教会中更高的地位。

texts.en:
"That's quite enough, my child," the curate says with iron concealed beneath soft words, "Perhaps you should undertake a prayer of contrition in the chapel while I speak with the captain."

Abashed, the attendant bows and flees. The curate turns to you and says, "Please accept my apologies. I shall personally show you the way to the inner shrine."
texts.zh:
"够了，我的孩子，" 祭司轻柔的话语里透露出铁一般的执着，"也许在我和舰长说话时，你应该在小教堂里做一个忏悔的祈祷。"

羞愧不堪的圣务侍急忙弯下腰，逃也似地离开了。祭司转向你说，"请接受我的道歉。我会亲自带你去内部圣地的。"

options.en: On second thought, show me the interior shrine.
options.zh: 仔细想想，还是带我看看内部的圣地吧。

options.en: Yes. I wish to go outside.

texts.en:
The air hits you in the environmental lock, warm and wet, like high-G shock foam. You step out alone, for this is how it is done.

Oozing nets hang from the shrine complex; rhizomes sprouting luridly colored bulbs that glow in what passes for sunlight. Dust, or tiny bugs, or spores float about, moving in swirls against the heavy and languid air.
texts.zh:
湿热的空气从直通外界环境的气闸里喷涌而出，如同高 G 力缓冲泡沫那样猛烈冲击你的身体。你独自迈步而出，正如仪式要求的那般。

圣地的殿堂上挂满了蛛网，植物的根茎上长出五彩斑斓的球团，在勉强能算是阳光的事物之下闪闪发亮。那些尘埃，微虫，又或者是孢子的东西，四处漂浮着，顶着沉重而慵懒的空气打起旋来。

options.en: Take off your mask. Have faith.
Keep it on, you're not an idiot.
options.zh: 戴好面罩，你又不是傻子。

texts.en:
You reach up and loose your mask, drawing in breath from Jangala. Shallowly at first, then deeper. The smells of spice and rot and ammonia and fresh greens. Whatever may come, you know it won't instantly kill you, and anything that happens is reversible. Is that a tingle, a catch in your throat?

Have faith.

You follow the short trail you were told of. It seems nearly overgrown, feelers and tendrils brush against you.

There are others. Maskless pilgrims, tears streaming from their red eyes and mucus from their noses, skin blotchy, white robes rapidly discolored by alien emissions. They meet your eyes, smile and nod in camaraderie, making the signs of Ludd for you.
texts.zh:
你抬手揭下面罩，吞吐着 Jangala 的气息。从刚开始的轻浅试探，逐渐变得深吸长气。香辛味，腐败味，氨味，新鲜绿植味，百味杂陈。不论迎面扑来的是什么气体，你知道这都不会让你当场毙命，而且造成的损伤都是可逆的。然而你喉头依然感到一丝异样，是刺痛吗？

秉持信仰。

你照着自己得知的那条捷径走了下去。这条路看起来几乎全都是杂草，触角和卷须不断刮蹭着你。

这里还有其他的人。那是些摘掉面罩的朝圣者，他们双眼通红，涕泗横流，皮肤斑驳，一袭白袍在异星的废气里迅速褪色。他们与你目光相交，怀揣着同道的情谊对你微笑颔首，行卢德之礼。

texts.en:
There are overgrown human figures - a statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting the fruiting bodies of alien life.

One moves; not the wind, but another pilgrim, the growths taking hold. How long does this take, hours? Days?

It becomes distracting, hard to focus. You feel like you might die, but the feeling reaches a plateau, a sea of pain and irritation. You allow yourself to float in a buzzing atonal headache, itchiness, torment.

And something more.
texts.zh:
这里到处植物漫身的人形 —— 简直是一座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了外星生命的子实体。

周围传来了一阵动静，不是风吹草动，而是另一个朝圣者被植物的疯长给牢牢抓住了。这要花多长时间？几个小时，还是几天？

这些景象让人精神溃散，难以保持专注。你感到自己可能会就这样死去，但这种感觉上升到了极限之后就不再积累，形成了一片充满了痛苦和焦虑的汪洋。你任由自己漂浮这一片杂乱无章且挥之不去的头痛，瘙痒和折磨之中。

以及一些别的东西...

texts.en:
The green churns imperceptibly, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.

And you are within it, for all of its horror and comfort.
texts.zh:
绿色在难以察觉地翻腾着，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

而你正置身其中，感受着它的震撼与慰藉。

texts.en:
You follow the short trail you were told of; it seems nearly overgrown. You follow it, feelers and tendrils brushing against you.

There are others. Maskless pilgrims, tears streaming from their red eyes and mucus from their noses, skin blotchy, white robes rapidly discolored by alien emissions.

You breathe shallowly. Is your skin hotter, dryer; wetter? Is that itch something taking hold? Whatever may come, you know it won't instantly kill you, and anything that happens is reversible. Have faith.
texts.zh:
你沿着被告知的短途小径前进；它看起来杂草丛生，藤蔓和卷须刮蹭着你的身体。

这里也有其他摘下了面罩的朝圣者，他们双眼通红，涕泗横流，皮肤斑驳，一袭白袍在异星的废气里迅速褪色。

你浅浅地呼吸，感受着环境的影响。皮肤变得燥热还是干裂又或是湿润？隐约还有不断变强的瘙痒？不过你知道，无论将要发生什么，都不会让你当场毙命，并且所有的损伤都是可逆的。秉持信仰。

texts.en:
Beyond, you see the statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting fruiting bodies of xenolife. Among them are pilgrims, exposed in their light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth. How long does it take- hours, days?

At their feet, covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium or alien equivalents, are bones. Or are they fallen branches, overgrown rocks? The final wish for terminally-devoted fanatics, or your imagination?
texts.zh:
远处，你看见一座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了异种生命的子实体。穿着浅色长袍的朝圣者们夹杂在其中。过度生长的植物轻松的淹没了他们。形成这一切花费了多少时间？是几个小时，还是数天？

他们的脚下，那被苔藓和菌丝或类似外星生物组成的被子覆盖着的，是骨头，还是枯枝，乱石？是狂热信徒的遗愿，或者只是你自己的想象？

texts.en: The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of your stay, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh: 在你逗留的这段时间里，这些绿植微不可查地翻搅着，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

texts.en: You make your way toward the landing pads, past pilgrims queuing for the charity cafeteria, regrouping before or after visiting the shrine, and otherwise stowing their humble possessions.
texts.zh: 你朝着停机坪走去，路过在慈善食堂前排队的朝圣者。他们或在参拜圣地前后重新聚集，又或者在收起他们微不足道的财物。

texts.en: "Bringing oneself before the sacred is not a matter of convenience," the attendant says serenely. "That we must travail so to worship here confers upon the act an extraordinary sense of self-reflection, I believe."
texts.zh: "虔诚的人会追寻信仰，哪怕千辛万苦。" 圣务侍平静地说，"我相信，我们必须经历苦难才有资格在这里朝拜，这会带来一种非凡的自我反思意识。"

options.en: I hear some pilgrims go outside unprotected.
options.zh: 我听说有些朝圣者在没有保护的情况下就出去了。

options.en: I would like to visit the shrine.

texts.en:
"Perhaps." The attendant cools a little, "As Ludd said, 'To hold faith in your heart, wholly and truly, invites small cruelties of the tongue's lash.'"

"And do you know what Ludd said next?," they ask, rhetorically, "'Let faith be your armor; let walls of devotion build you a citadel, and there we shall be always in spiritual union.'"

The attendant seems satisfied with the unassailability of this statement, and wishing to hurry you along before things get more awkward, adds "Is there anything else I may assist you with?"
texts.zh:
"也许吧。" 圣务侍冷静了一点，"正如卢德所言，'真心全意地坚守信仰，往往会招致流言蜚语的恶意中伤。'"

"你知道卢德接下来说了什么吗？" 他反问道，"'让信仰成为你的铠甲；让虔诚化作无数城墙，为你构成堡垒，如此一来，我们的灵魂就能永远合为一体。'"

圣务侍看起来对这句话的无懈可击感到满意。为了赶快结束话题以避免尴尬，他补充道："还有什么我可以帮助你的吗？"

options.en: I'd like to visit the shrine.

texts.en: "Yes, that is true." The attendant cools a little, questioning your motives. "We try to discourage, ah, sightseers. It disturbs the worship, you see."
texts.zh: "是的，确有其事。" 圣务侍稍微冷静了一点，怀疑你来此的目的。"我们试图劝阻这些，呃，游客。你知道的，这干扰了朝拜。"

options.en: I am no sightseer, but I do want to undertake this experience.
options.zh: 我不是游客，但我确实想体验一下。

options.en: I am no sightseer. I wish to test my faith.
options.zh: 我不是游客。我想考验自己的信念。

options.en: Don't worry, I have no intention of going out there.
options.zh: 别担心，我没有要出去的意思。

texts.en:
The attendant looks at you with new respect.

"You are sure of this, pilgrim? You desire this with full knowledge of what exposure to Jangala entails, and choose to take this holy suffering upon your body?"
texts.zh:
圣务侍以前所未有的敬意看着你。

"你确定吗，朝圣者？你渴望接触 Jangala ，同时充分了解这会带来什么，并选择将这份神圣的痛苦施于自身？"

texts.en:
The hum of your shuttle changes pitch as it hits the edge of true atmosphere, passing quickly into cloud cover. Beyond the viewpanes human-eye visibility is reduced to nearly zero. As the shuttle fires retros for landing, dipping well below the speed of sound by the demand of both nav regs and good manners, your viewport begins to collect marching droplets of moisture.

The droplets have an odd ochre coloration, and the clouds above a sickly green tinge. You've heard of this effect; fine-grained spore-analogs in the atmosphere.
texts.zh:
伴随着时高时低的噪音，你的穿梭机抵达了真实大气的边缘，一瞬间消失在云层之中。在观察窗之外，人眼的能见度几乎为零。当穿梭机开始着陆时，由于导航规则和礼貌的要求，其下降速度远低于音速，你的观察窗逐渐布满移动着的水滴。

水滴呈现出一种奇怪的赭色，而云层上方又是病态的绿色。你对此有所耳闻：这是大气中细小的类孢子的东西。

options.en: Look up the long term effects of the spores
options.zh: 查阅这些孢子的长期影响

texts.en:
Your shuttle descends to the landing pad, the Jangalan foliage encroaching through its own ashes to reclaim the space.

You pop a standard dose of antixenols and re-examine the quality of your breathing mask as the access tunnel takes a moment to perform a self-cleaning cycle on exposed surfaces. The air feels no different, yet.

Maybe a little warmer, a little heavier with moisture.
texts.zh:
你的穿梭机刚降落在停机坪，Jangala 上的植物就重新开始在自己的灰烬上生长，夺回了属于它们的领地。

人行通道需要一段时间对裸露的表面进行自清洁循环，你趁此时注射了标准剂量的抗异种药物，并重新检查呼吸面罩的质量。尽管这里的空气感觉也没什么不同。

也许也就是更暖和、更潮湿一点。

texts.en:
A quick datapad search reveals that, statistically, human activity within the Jangalan biosphere is relatively safe so long as proper air filtration and decontamination procedures are followed. Detox meds for accidental exposures are readily available, though may have unpleasant side effects.

There are reports of individuals whose poor luck and lack of contingency planning combined with vehicle malfunction during truly abysmal weather has resulted in cases of long term exposure to Jangala's biosphere for days, weeks, and in one case more than a standard month. The resulting growths and infections appear to result in a singularly torturous manner of death.
texts.zh:
数据平板的快速检索显示，从统计数据来看，只要遵循适当的空气过滤和净化程序，Jangala 生物圈内的人类活动相对安全。针对意外暴露的排毒药物很容易获取，尽管它们可能产生令人不快的副作用。

有报道称，一些人的运气不佳，缺乏应急计划，再加上在真正恶劣的天气下的载具故障，导致他们长期暴露在 Jangala 生物圈达数天、数周，有一例甚至超过一个标准月。由此产生的生长和感染似乎导致了异常折磨的死亡。

texts.en:
-At least, judging by the holos available on the public infonet, which are indeed gruesome.

A cynical part of you wonders if the authorities allow distribution of these graphic accounts to promote protocol compliance.
texts.zh:
—— 至少，从公共信息网上的全息图来看，这确实很可怕。

你心里突然泛起一丝愤世嫉俗的想法，在想当局是否在故意放任这些图片的传播，就是为了促使人们遵守安全规定。

options.en: Take a shuttle to visit the Luddic shrine
options.zh: 乘坐穿梭机前去拜访卢德圣地

options.en: Take a shuttle to visit the Luddic shrine
options.zh: 乘坐穿梭机前去拜访卢德圣地

texts.en:
Your shuttle descends toward verdant continents crowned by lethargically churning storm systems. The orbital burn lasers flicker from the spark of Jangala station, invisible until they cut lines of plasma through the atmosphere.

You pass through blinding cloud cover, the light taking on a sickly hue of green. Your viewport is streaked with marching droplets of spore-laden water as the shuttle slows to drop softly onto the landing pad nearly lost in the overgrowth of Jangalan foliage.
texts.zh:
你的穿梭机降落在苍翠的陆地上，翻腾的风暴在地表缓慢移动着。伴随着 Jangala 空间站上闪烁的光斑，轨道激光倾泻而下，在大气层中切出耀眼的等离子火焰。

你穿过炫目的云层，映入眼帘的是一片令人头晕的绿色。舷窗外，饱含孢子的雨滴如行军般奔流而下；穿梭机减速缓降，轻柔地停靠在几乎被 Jangala 疯长的植被彻底吞没的停机坪上。

texts.en:
The verdant continents of Jangala sprawl beneath you, crowned by huge weather systems churning lethargic and magisterial.

Searing lines of orbital burn lasers flick out from Jangala station, invisible until they cut slashes of plasma through the thick atmosphere. Burn-glow competes with rampaging electrical storms to illuminate the mountainous cloud formations from below.
texts.zh:
Jangala 青翠的大陆在你脚下延伸，巨型的云层在你的头顶上慵懒地翻腾着。

炽热的轨道激光从 Jangala 空间站中喷涌而出，在大气层中划出一道道炫目的等离子体。燃烧的辉光和云层中的闪电交相辉映，照亮了下面那些如山峦般厚重的云层。

texts.en:
The reception lounge is filled with parties of Luddic pilgrims in traditional handweave led by subcurates in ritual hand-washing. A glance upward reveals the true cleansing: a battery of air-purification units caught in a tangle of murmuring ducts.

Foliage presses itself almost sensually against the outer viewports, letting in only dim light. The plant life seems to twitch, liquids oozing over the panes from cracks in bladders and tubules, leaving rivulets cutting across flaking encrustations. Between the zeal of the foliage and hand-crafted charm of Luddic engineering, the place feels distinctly worrisome compared to the environmental containment you are accustomed to.
texts.zh:
接待休息室里挤满了在此聚会的卢德朝圣者。他们身着传统的手工服装，由助理祭司带领进行仪式性的净手。向上看一眼，你就会发现这里真正的清洁设施：淹没在复杂管道中的一组空气净化装置。

舞动着的叶片几乎堵死了窗户，只有些许昏暗的光线照射进来。这些富有生机的植物似乎在抽搐着，液体从囊状器官和小管的裂缝中渗出，留下一条条涓涓细流划过剥落的外壳。在植物的躁动和卢德工艺的魅力之间，与你习惯的，那些被精心调控的环境相比，这个地方明显令人担忧。

texts.en:
One of the shrine's attendants instantly recognizes that you're not one of the usual pilgrims and intercepts you, making remarkable speed despite wearing awkward-looking novice's robes.

The attendant smiles piously, hands held together. "How might we assist you?"
texts.zh:
圣地的一名圣务侍立即意识到你不是寻常的朝圣者。尽管穿着看起来很尴尬的新手长袍，他还是很快地拦住了你。

圣务侍双手合十，虔诚地微笑着。"我们能为您提供什么帮助？"

options.en: I'd like to visit the shrine.
I wish to visit the shrine. Outside.
options.zh: 我希望参拜圣地。在户外。

texts.en:
One of the shrine's attendants scurries to meet you.

"The complex is kept overpressurized," they say, following your gaze, "so if there were a breach, there would be plenty of time to find and seal the leak."

The attendant creates what must be intended to be a reassuring smile. "How might we assist you?"
texts.zh:
圣地的圣务侍赶忙出来迎接你。

"这片建筑群一直处于超载状态，" 跟随着你的目光，他们说道，"所以，如果哪里有漏洞，我们应该能有足够的时间发现并将其密封。"

圣务侍做出一个令人安心的笑容。"我们能为您提供什么帮助？"

texts.en: "Bringing oneself before the sacred is not a matter of convenience," the attendant says serenely. "That we must travail so to worship here confers upon the act an extraordinary sense of self-reflection, I believe."

options.zh: 我听说有些朝圣者在没有保护的情况下就出去了。

options.zh: 我不是游客。我想考验自己的信念。

options.en: Don't worry, I have no intention of going out there.
options.zh: 别担心，我没有要出去的意思。

texts.en:
"Yes, of course. I can show you to the washing station where we ask that all, pilgrim or no, partake of a simple cleansing before visiting the interior shrine."

The attendant starts to shuffle you along into a group of devotees.
texts.zh:
"是，当然可以。我可以带你去净化站，在那里我们要求所有人，无论朝圣者与否，在参观圣地内部之前进行简单的清洁。"

圣务侍把你带进虔信者的队伍中。

options.en: I mean the outside. The real shrine.
options.zh: 我的意思是去外面，去真正的圣地。

texts.en:
The attendant looks you over skeptically.

"You are sure of this? You desire this with full knowledge of what exposure to Jangala entails?"

The attendant brings your attention to a row of pamphlets in a tasteful wooden stand displaying what, at a glance, appear to be a selection of truly unholy skin conditions.
texts.zh:
圣务侍一脸疑惑地看着你。

"你认真的？你真的了解暴露在 Jangala 的地表会造成什么后果吗？"

圣务侍示意你留意一旁的雅致木架，上面展示了一排翻开了的宣传册。你瞥了一眼，看来里面应该是精选了各种非常不神圣的皮肤感染症状。

texts.en:
The attendant looks at you with new respect.

"You are sure of this, pilgrim? You desire this with full knowledge of what exposure to Jangala entails, and choose to take this holy suffering upon your body?"
texts.zh:
圣务侍以前所未有的敬意看着你。

"你确定吗，朝圣者？你渴望接触 Jangala ，同时充分了解这会带来什么，并选择将这份神圣的痛苦施于自身？"

options.en: On second thought, show me the interior shrine.
options.zh: 仔细想想，还是带我看看内部的圣地吧。

options.en: Yes. I wish to go outside.

texts.en:
"Would it not be 'foolish', captain, to expose yourself to the outside?" the attendant says, somehow keeping peevishness out of their tone if not words.

As if on cue - or perhaps because they were hovering nearby the whole time - a curate (you presume) of the shrine steps up to you and the attendant, robes not quite resplendent but conveying a sense of care and craft that belies a higher status in the Church.
texts.zh:
"把自己暴露在外面不是很 '愚蠢' 吗，舰长？" 圣务侍说。不知为何，他的语气并不焦躁。

就好像是在暗示，或者可能是因为他们一直在附近徘徊，一位圣地的祭司 (你推测) 走到你和圣务侍面前。他的长袍并不那么华丽，但传达了一种谨慎和诡秘的感觉，这掩盖了他们在教会中更高的地位。

texts.en:
"That's quite enough, my child," the curate says with iron concealed beneath soft words, "Perhaps you should undertake a prayer of contrition in the chapel while I speak with the captain."

Abashed, the attendant bows and flees. The curate turns to you and says, "Please accept my apologies. I shall personally show you the way to the inner shrine."
texts.zh:
"够了，我的孩子，" 祭司轻柔的话语里透露出铁一般的执着，"也许在我和舰长说话时，你应该在小教堂里做一个忏悔的祈祷。"

羞愧不堪的圣务侍急忙弯下腰，逃也似地离开了。祭司转向你说，"请接受我的道歉。我会亲自带你去内部圣地的。"

texts.en:
You are led past heavy curtains. The murmur of pilgrims is muted, and all artificial light shut out.

Your eyes adjust to the shrine-chamber, taking in rows of silhouetted pilgrims kneeling before polished panes of diamond-matrix, illuminated by the sickly yellow-green cloud cover from without.

Beyond the windows, you see overgrown human figures - a statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting the fruiting bodies of alien life. One moves; not the wind, but another pilgrim, exposed and outdoors. There are people out there, you realize with a start, wearing only light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth.
texts.zh:
你被带领着穿过厚重的幕布。朝圣者的窃窃私语沉寂了下来，所有的人造光源都被熄灭了。

你刚适应神殿内的昏暗光线，就看到一排排的朝圣者跪倒在金刚石方窗前。它们的侧影被外面病态的黄绿色云层所照亮。

在窗外，你看到被植物寄生的人形 —— 那是一座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了外星生命的子实体。其中一个人形移动着 —— 那不是风在吹动，而是另一个在户外的朝圣者。你猛然意识到，外面的人只穿着浅色长袍，这使得他们很容易隐蔽在植物群中。

texts.en:
At their feet, more forms come into focus; covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium, or whatever alien equivalent, which obscures the feet of the statues. Bones. Or are they fallen branches and overgrown rocks? The final wish for some terminally-devoted fanatics, or your imagination set loose?

The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of the minutes you watch, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh:
在他们脚下，更多种类的植物映入眼帘；苔藓和菌丝，或者其他类似的东西，覆盖着雕像的脚。那是人骨，还是倒下的树枝和杂草丛生的岩石？这是一些狂热者的终极渴望，又或者仅仅是你的想象？

在你观察的几分钟里，你并不难察觉到那些搅动着的绿色，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

texts.en:
You are led past heavy curtains which mute the murmur of pilgrims and shut out all artificial light. Pilgrims kneel in the shrine-chamber, silhouetted before the glowing panes to without lit by that sickly yellow-green cloud cover.

Beyond, you see the statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting fruiting bodies of xenolife. Among them are pilgrims, exposed in only light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth. At their feet, covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium or alien equivalents, are bones. Or are they fallen branches, overgrown rocks? The final wish for terminally-devoted fanatics, or your imagination?

The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of the minutes you watch, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh:
你被带领着穿过厚重的幕布，这些布料阻隔了朝圣者的低语，挡住了所有的人造光源。朝圣者们跪倒在神殿内，他们在明亮的窗格前被勾勒出轮廓，不必被那病态的黄绿色云层照亮。

在远处，你看到了那座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了异种生命的子实体。只穿着浅色长袍的朝圣者夹杂其中，疯长的植物轻易淹没了他们。在他们脚下，那被苔藓和菌丝或类似外星生物组成的被子覆盖着的是人骨，还是倒下的树枝和杂乱的岩石？是绝境中狂热信徒的最后愿望，又或者仅仅是你的想象？

在你停留的几分钟里，绿色在不知不觉中汹涌澎湃，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

texts.en:
The air hits you in the environmental lock, warm and wet, like high-G shock foam. You step out alone, for this is how it is done.

Oozing nets hang from the shrine complex; rhizomes sprouting luridly colored bulbs that glow in what passes for sunlight. Dust, or tiny bugs, or spores float about, moving in swirls against the heavy and languid air.
texts.zh:
湿热的空气从直通外界环境的气闸里喷涌而出，如同高 G 力缓冲泡沫那样猛烈冲击你的身体。你独自迈步而出，正如仪式要求的那般。

圣地的殿堂上挂满了蛛网，植物的根茎上长出五彩斑斓的球团，在勉强能算是阳光的事物之下闪闪发亮。那些尘埃，微虫，又或者是孢子的东西，四处漂浮着，顶着沉重而慵懒的空气打起旋来。

options.en: Take off your mask. Have faith.
Keep it on, you're not an idiot.
options.zh: 戴好面罩，你又不是傻子。

texts.en:
You reach up and loose your mask, drawing in breath from Jangala. Shallowly at first, then deeper. The smells of spice and rot and ammonia and fresh greens. Whatever may come, you know it won't instantly kill you, and anything that happens is reversible. Is that a tingle, a catch in your throat?

Have faith.

You follow the short trail you were told of. It seems nearly overgrown, feelers and tendrils brush against you.

There are others. Maskless pilgrims, tears streaming from their red eyes and mucus from their noses, skin blotchy, white robes rapidly discolored by alien emissions. They meet your eyes, smile and nod in camaraderie, making the signs of Ludd for you.
texts.zh:
你抬手揭下面罩，吞吐着 Jangala 的气息。从刚开始的轻浅试探，逐渐变得深吸长气。香辛味，腐败味，氨味，新鲜绿植味，百味杂陈。不论迎面扑来的是什么气体，你知道这都不会让你当场毙命，而且造成的损伤都是可逆的。然而你喉头依然感到一丝异样，是刺痛吗？

秉持信仰。

你照着自己得知的那条捷径走了下去。这条路看起来几乎全都是杂草，触角和卷须不断刮蹭着你。

这里还有其他的人。那是些摘掉面罩的朝圣者，他们双眼通红，涕泗横流，皮肤斑驳，一袭白袍在异星的废气里迅速褪色。他们与你目光相交，怀揣着同道的情谊对你微笑颔首，行卢德之礼。

texts.en:
There are overgrown human figures - a statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting the fruiting bodies of alien life.

One moves; not the wind, but another pilgrim, the growths taking hold. How long does this take, hours? Days?

It becomes distracting, hard to focus. You feel like you might die, but the feeling reaches a plateau, a sea of pain and irritation. You allow yourself to float in a buzzing atonal headache, itchiness, torment.

And something more.
texts.zh:
这里到处植物漫身的人形 —— 简直是一座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了外星生命的子实体。

周围传来了一阵动静，不是风吹草动，而是另一个朝圣者被植物的疯长给牢牢抓住了。这要花多长时间？几个小时，还是几天？

这些景象让人精神溃散，难以保持专注。你感到自己可能会就这样死去，但这种感觉上升到了极限之后就不再积累，形成了一片充满了痛苦和焦虑的汪洋。你任由自己漂浮这一片杂乱无章且挥之不去的头痛，瘙痒和折磨之中。

以及一些别的东西...

texts.en:
The green churns imperceptibly, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.

And you are within it, for all of its horror and comfort.
texts.zh:
绿色在难以察觉地翻腾着，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

而你正置身其中，感受着它的震撼与慰藉。

texts.en:
You follow the short trail you were told of; it seems nearly overgrown. You follow it, feelers and tendrils brushing against you.

There are others. Maskless pilgrims, tears streaming from their red eyes and mucus from their noses, skin blotchy, white robes rapidly discolored by alien emissions.

You breathe shallowly. Is your skin hotter, dryer; wetter? Is that itch something taking hold? Whatever may come, you know it won't instantly kill you, and anything that happens is reversible. Have faith.
texts.zh:
你沿着被告知的短途小径前进；它看起来杂草丛生，藤蔓和卷须刮蹭着你的身体。

这里也有其他摘下了面罩的朝圣者，他们双眼通红，涕泗横流，皮肤斑驳，一袭白袍在异星的废气里迅速褪色。

你浅浅地呼吸，感受着环境的影响。皮肤变得燥热还是干裂又或是湿润？隐约还有不断变强的瘙痒？不过你知道，无论将要发生什么，都不会让你当场毙命，并且所有的损伤都是可逆的。秉持信仰。

texts.en:
Beyond, you see the statue garden. The forms blister with growths, crawling with tendrils, sprouting fruiting bodies of xenolife. Among them are pilgrims, exposed in their light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth. How long does it take- hours, days?

At their feet, covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium or alien equivalents, are bones. Or are they fallen branches, overgrown rocks? The final wish for terminally-devoted fanatics, or your imagination?
texts.zh:
远处，你看见一座雕像花园。这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了异种生命的子实体。穿着浅色长袍的朝圣者们夹杂在其中。过度生长的植物轻松的淹没了他们。形成这一切花费了多少时间？是几个小时，还是数天？

他们的脚下，那被苔藓和菌丝或类似外星生物组成的被子覆盖着的，是骨头，还是枯枝，乱石？是狂热信徒的遗愿，或者只是你自己的想象？

texts.en: The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of your stay, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh: 在你逗留的这段时间里，这些绿植微不可查地翻搅着，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

texts.en: You undergo a routine decontamination in a stained yet clean chamber built for that purpose. After an oddly-smelling shower, the flicker of lasers, and another round of antixenols, you are given back your clothing. Everything is abrasively dry and smells of disinfectant.
texts.zh: 你在一间整洁但略有污渍的洁净室里接受了例行去污。穿过气味奇怪的淋浴、照过几次激光、又服用了另一轮抗异种感染药物之后，你拿回了你的衣服。所有东西都被强力烘干过，还带着点消毒液的味道。

texts.en: Breathing feels strange, still. You have to think about each breath, filling your lungs, then emptying them.
texts.zh: 呼吸的感觉仍然很奇怪。你不得不仔细进行每一次呼吸，用空气填满你的肺，然后排空它们。

texts.en:
The air hits you, warm and wet, like high-G shock foam. You step out and follow the short trail; it seems nearly overgrown. You follow it, leaves and feelers brushing against you.

You find the statue gardens, the forms blistering with growth, crawling with tendrils, sprouting fruiting bodies of xenolife. Among them are pilgrims, exposed in their light robes. Easily overtaken by the overgrowth. How long does it take- hours, days?

At their feet, covered by a quilt of mosses and mycelium or alien equivalents, are bones. Or fallen branches, overgrown rocks. Or the final wish for terminally-devoted fanatics.

The green churns not quite imperceptibly in the course of your stay, all-consuming, ferociously regenerative, a cycle of life that could be born of Earth or an alien world.
texts.zh:
空气刺痛着你，带来温暖又潮湿的感觉，就像高重力缓冲泡沫一样。你沿着小路走了出去，这条路几乎被植物淹没了。你顺着路继续前行，树叶和触须拂过你的身体。

你发现了一座雕像花园，这些造像身上缀满了液疱，缠满了卷须，萌发出了异种生命的子实体。穿着浅色长袍的朝圣者夹杂其中，疯长的植物轻易淹没了他们。形成这一切花费了多少时间？是几个小时，还是数天？

他们的脚下，那被苔藓和菌丝或类似外星生物组成的被子覆盖着的，是骨头，还是枯枝，乱石？是狂热信徒的遗愿，或者只是你自己的想象？

在你停留的几分钟里，绿色在不知不觉中汹涌澎湃，无厌地吞噬，凶蛮地再生，生命的轮回既可以生于地球，也可以生于一个异星世界。

options.en: Return to the interior of the complex

texts.en: You make your way toward the landing pads, past pilgrims queuing for the charity cafeteria, regrouping before or after visiting the shrine, and otherwise stowing their humble possessions.
texts.zh: 你朝着停机坪走去，路过在慈善食堂前排队的朝圣者。他们或在参拜圣地前后重新聚集，又或者在收起他们微不足道的财物。

texts.en: You make your way toward the landing pads, past pilgrims queuing for the charity cafeteria, regrouping before or after visiting the shrine, and otherwise stowing their humble possessions.
texts.zh: 你朝着停机坪走去，路过在慈善食堂前排队的朝圣者。他们或在参拜圣地前后重新聚集，又或者在收起他们微不足道的财物。

options.en: Take a shuttle to visit the Luddic shrine
options.zh: 乘坐穿梭机前去拜访卢德圣地

texts.en:
You are just beginning to make your way toward the shuttle bay when you receive a ping from your nav officer: the request to land has been denied by traffic control.

Strange. This should be perfectly routine.
texts.zh:
你刚刚开始前往穿梭机停泊港便收到了你领航军官的消息：着陆请求被交通管制中心拒绝了。

奇怪。这请求再普通不过了。

texts.en:
You put in the order to have a shuttle prepared for a flight to the surface.

"Captain," your Nav officer reports, "Traffic control is denying your flight request."
texts.zh:
你下令让一艘穿梭机做好飞往地面的准备。

"舰长，" 你的领航军官汇报道，"交通管制处否决了你的飞行请求。"

texts.en:
You put in the order to have a shuttle prepared for a flight to the surface.

"Captain," your Nav officer reports, "Traffic control is denying your flight request."
texts.zh:
你下令让一艘穿梭机做好飞往地面的准备。

"舰长，" 你的领航军官汇报道，"交通管制处否决了你的飞行请求。"

options.en: Request to speak with someone in authority
Get me the Excubitor Orbis on comms.
Get me the Excubitor Orbis on comms.

texts.en:
"Affirmative," Nav says. A moments pause. "Captain, I have traffic control on comms."

Nav patches you into the comm-loop, and a young-looking Luddic Knight, probably an initiate, appears before you.
texts.zh:
"好的，" 领航员说到。片刻过后。"舰长，我已经接通了交通管制中心。"

领航员将你接入到通讯回路中，一个看起来很年轻的卢德骑士，可能是个新人，出现在了你的面前。

texts.en:
"Blessed for the day, Captain," they just manage to hide the quaver in their voice. "With apologies, your request to land has been denied."

As you draw breath to reply, the initiate's eyes flick to a notification and go wide.

"Apologies, Captain ... I mean, respectfully. I... the Excubitor Orbis wishes to speak with you," they say without stumbling on the title. Practice, you're sure.

"Transferring link."
texts.zh:
"愿卢德保佑你，舰长。" 他们成功地藏住了他们声音中的颤抖，"十分抱歉，你的着陆请求被拒绝了。"

你吸了一口气，正准备回复，这个新人瞧了一眼通知然后瞪大了他的眼睛。

"抱歉，舰长... 我的意思是，尊敬的。我想说... 行星教卫想要和你通话。" 他们在念头衔的时候倒是十分流利。练过，你很确信。

"正在转接。"

texts.en:
The Excubitor Orbis appears before you.

"Captain $playerName," he says by way of greeting, a stern gaze already fixed on you.

The moment draws longer. He is the image of poise, perfectly content to wait for you to speak. A wrinkle appears, then disappears, by a mouth which appears fixed permanently on the precipice of a frown.
texts.zh:
行星教卫出现在了你的面前。

"$playerName 舰长。" 他以问候的语气说道，同时严肃地盯着你。

时间的流逝仿佛变慢了。他就好像是沉着的化身，全然沉浸于对你的等待之中。嘴角的皱纹若隐若现，像是被永远困在了成型的边缘不断徘徊。

options.en: Why was my travel request denied?
options.zh: 为什么我的航行请求被拒绝了？

options.en: I demand to know why my request was denied!
options.zh: 我要求得知为什么我的请求被拒绝了！

texts.en:
"I ordered your landing request denied," he states plainly. "The protection of this world is my duty."

"I find that those with a history of exceptional acts oft test the charity of Providence by taking exceptional risks."
texts.zh:
"我下令拒绝了你的降落请求，"他开门见山地说道，"保护这个世界是我的职责。"

"我发现那些有着非凡过往的人经常冒着巨大风险来试探上天的慈悲。"

options.en: So I need to convince you that I am not a risk?
options.zh: 所以我需要让你相信我不是一个风险？

options.en: Are you accusing me of criminal intent?
options.zh: 你在指控我拥有犯罪倾向吗？

options.en:
Just tell me how many credits I need to 'tithe'.
#lpp_hesperusExcubitorForce:"With my fleet, how can you stop me?"
options.zh:
告诉我需要缴纳多少 '什一税' 就好。
#lpp_hesperusExcubitorForce:"你要怎样阻止我和我的舰队？"

texts.en:
That wrinkle again, the Sector's smallest smile.

"Spend not your time in this life on folly; even our youngest initiate could see that you wear risk like a badge. The secular procedures at hand are only part of my purview," he says.

"At present I am more concerned with your spirit."
texts.zh:
那个皱纹 —— 或者也可以说是全星域最微弱的笑容 —— 又一次浮现出来。

"奉劝你，此生莫要行愚蠢之事。纵使我等最年轻的新教友也可看出，你危险常伴，有如勋章在身。手头的那些红尘琐事，毕竟只是我职责的冰山一角。" 他说道。

"此时此刻，我更关注你心中的真意。"

texts.en: He drops a heavy hand like a gavel on his desk. "I am uninterested in more words. Listen well now, for I speak my judgment on this matter."
texts.zh: 他像落下拍卖锤一般重重地拍了一下桌子。"我不想再听下去了。现在，好好听我对这件事的判断吧。"

texts.en:
"Your reputation is suspect, captain. I cannot in good conscience allow you access to our shrine," the Excubitor Orbis says. "Find yourself redemption. If you manage to find some degree of it, then we may discuss the matter again."

"Seek virtue, captain," he says by way of farewell.
texts.zh:
"你的恶名让人产生怀疑，舰长。我不能问心无愧地让你访问我们的圣地。" 行星教卫说到，"为你自己寻找救赎吧。如果你能多少找到一些，那我们可以再讨论一下这件事。"

"求善，舰长。" 他以告别的语气说到。

texts.en:
A long pause.

"I shall order traffic control to give you permission to land, captain," the Excubitor Orbis says finally. "May your spirit find that for which it searches."
texts.zh:
通讯频道陷入了长久的沉默。

"我会让交通管制中心给予你降落许可，舰长。" 行星教卫终于开口，"愿你的灵魂能寻找到它所追寻之物。"

texts.en:
"I shall review your request in seven days," the Excubitor Orbis says. "If that is enough for Creation, it will be enough for you to learn patience."

That wrinkle again.

"Blessings be, captain."
texts.zh:
"我将在七天之内审核你的请求，" 行星教卫说到。"如果这时间足够创造天地万物，那么也足够让你学习到耐心。"

他脸上再次浮现出充满褶皱的笑。

"愿你蒙福，舰长。"

options.en: How about we talk about redemption now.
options.zh: 不如我们现在就谈谈救赎吧。

texts.en: You cut the comm link.
texts.zh: 你切断了通讯链接。

texts.en: You cut the comm link.
texts.zh: 你切断了通讯链接。

texts.en:
That wrinkle again, the Sector's smallest smile.

"Yes, I am quite certain that you have committed many crimes. Secular justice is only part of my purview however," he says gravely.

"Today I am more concerned with your spirit."
texts.zh:
那个皱纹 —— 或者也可以说是全星域最微弱的笑容 —— 又一次浮现出来。

他严肃地说道："的确，我十分肯定，你犯下了诸多罪行。然而，世俗正义不过是我职责的冰山一角。"

"今日，我更关注你心中的真意。"

texts.en:
That wrinkle again, the Sector's smallest smile.

"How debased is our devotion that you would think saying those words would open the path before you."

"And," he continues, "How debased is your spiritual being that you would think to indulge it."
texts.zh:
那个皱纹 —— 或者也可以说是全星域最微弱的笑容 —— 又一次浮现出来。

"我等的奉献是何其卑贱，以至于让你认为那番话语就可为你开通前路。"

"而至于你，" 他继续道，"你的精神又是何其堕落，才会想着沉溺于此。"

texts.en:
The silence extends, uncomfortably. He blinks, slowly.

He's really doing this. Some kind of test, or challenge. Are you going to let him win?

He isn't giving up. He continues to stare, absurdly, saying nothing. You notice the subtlest flicker in the image as the display corrects for signal fluctuation.
texts.zh:
令人不快的死寂延续着，他缓缓地眨了眨眼。

他居然真的在这么做，像是某种测试或者挑战。你要把胜利拱手相让吗？

他锲而不舍，他一言不发，继续荒唐地盯着。你注意到显示器校正信号波动时，图像产生了些许闪烁。

texts.en: You've played this game before, with Gargoyle. You know how to win. Stay strong.
texts.zh: 你以前就和 Gargoyle 玩过这个游戏，你知道该怎么赢 —— 坚持不懈。

options.en: Why was my travel request denied?
options.zh: 为什么我的航行请求被拒绝了？

options.en: I demand to know why my request was denied!
options.zh: 我要求得知为什么我的请求被拒绝了！

texts.en:
The hum of your ship grows in your ears, the sense of inhabiting your own body in a can hurtling around a gravity well, the incomprehensible webs of influence keeping you both in this place and in the constant dynamism of crisis.

Lower and higher dimensions twist and vibrate, a web conspiring to hold you up - or back - falling and clinging just so. Your technologies tap these invisible quirks of physics to keep you warm, keep you cool; your feet on the deck, the air flowing follow a rhythm, a meter. It is like music, in fact. If you listen carefully...

It would be impossible to speak, now.
texts.zh:
飞船的轰鸣在你耳中不断回响放大，让你意识到自己正身处于一个围绕重力井飞驰的铁罐头中。引力犹如无数无边的大网，让你困入动力持续变动的危局之中，滞留于此。

高低维度互相交织震荡着，一同合谋将你网住，当你即将下坠时将你举起，在你意欲爬升时把你拖住。你身边的各种科技仿佛在有节奏地敲打着种种无形的物理异象，使你保持温暖，让你脚踏实地，令空气保持循环，一切都充满了韵律。其实这犹如乐曲，只要你仔细去聆听...

此刻，难以言述。

texts.en:
You almost jump as the Excubitor Orbis speaks, pulling you back to the moment.

"You possess patience," he says. A new wrinkle appears beside his mouth; what passes for a smile among the Knights of Ludd, you suppose.

"I did not expect it of you."

You've won. Is this victory? It is an uncomfortable feeling.
texts.zh:
行星教卫突然开口，差点吓了你一跳，也将你的思绪拉回现实。

"你很有耐心。" 他说。他的嘴角边又浮现出一抹皱纹；你猜测这在卢德骑士团里可能算是一种笑容吧。

"我没料到你会有如此耐心。"

你赢了。但这真的算得上是胜利吗？这种感觉让你一阵不舒服。

texts.en: Nav patches you into the link, and a young-looking Luddic Knight - or maybe an initiate - appears before you.
texts.zh: 领航员将你接入链接，然后一个看起来很年轻的卢德骑士 —— 或者是个新人 —— 出现在你的面前。

texts.en: You order the shuttle to stand down. Who knows what these Luddics are on about this time.
texts.zh: You order the shuttle to stand down. Who knows what these Luddics are on about this time.

texts.en: Nav routes your comm-link to the local system network, and after what feels like a longer than necessary wait, the link finally establishes a connection.
texts.zh: 领航员将你的通讯链接路由到本地的系统网络中，在经过一段感觉上超出必要等待所需的时间后，连接终于被建立。

texts.en: You order the shuttle to stand down. It looks like Excubitor Oak is serious about making you wait seven days before you can access the shrine of Hesperus.
texts.zh: You order the shuttle to stand down. It looks like Excubitor Oak is serious about making you wait seven days before you can access the shrine of Hesperus.

texts.en: You order the shuttle to stand down. It looks like Excubitor Oak is serious about denying you access to the shrine of Hesperus until you 'seek redemption', whatever that means.
texts.zh: You order the shuttle to stand down. It looks like Excubitor Oak is serious about denying you access to the shrine of Hesperus until you 'seek redemption', whatever that means.

texts.en:
Traffic control gives you its blessing and your shuttle descends toward the unforgiving surface of Hesperus.

The planet is riven by glaciers like a network of scars on the battered hide of some ancient beast. Your flight path takes you toward one great canyon filled with a chaos of ice and stone, then a child-branch over which walls of dark rock loom. Now and again you spot the crumbling remains of industry, and among them the occasional lights of Knight-chartered enterprises and monastic communities.
texts.zh:
交通管制处为你送上了例行的 "卢德保佑"。你的穿梭机开始降落到冰冷无情的 Hesperus 地表。

Hesperus 的地表被冰川切割得四分五裂，如同一头上古凶兽伤痕累累的毛皮，疤痕勾连成网。你的航线将你带往一个巨大的峡谷，里面凌乱地堆砌着冰块和岩石。接着映入眼帘的是峡谷的一条分支，其上是若隐若现，有如无边城墙的漆黑巨石。你时不时看见摇摇欲坠的工业遗迹，其中间或闪烁着属于骑士特批企业和隐修社区的灯火。

texts.en:
Around one last turn of the canyon, the shrine complex appears, a bright spire of habitats, towers, and masts rising from the misty remains of a titanic atmospheric processing plant.

Your trained eye spots the likely positions of heavy weapon emplacements: too-clean cliff-faces at convenient angles, the suspiciously level floors of certain hanging valleys.
texts.zh:
在峡谷的最后一个拐角处，圣地的殿堂出现了。那是一座由栖息地，塔楼，旗杆簇拥而成的尖顶，灯火辉煌，从云山雾罩的巨型大气处理厂废墟中拔地而起。

你久经训练的眼光发现了一些可能布置有重武器的位置：角度适合射击且过于干净的峭壁，某些悬谷上平坦到可疑的地表。

texts.en:
The landing bay antechamber is a baroque gothic-militant display of post-industrial salvage. Dead suits of power armor stand at attention, weapons proudly displayed. Glowing between rivet-encrusted arches are scenes of battle and martyrdom done up in mosaic panes formed of fractured gems; structural diamond and colorful lenses recovered from mining lasers or reactor inspection ports.

The gallery is filled with parties of Luddic pilgrims dressed in traditional handweave meeting with shrine attendants.
texts.zh:
登陆台的前厅里堆砌着后工业时代的文物，展现出巴洛克式的艺术风格，以及哥特式的尚武。能源耗尽的动力装甲摆出立正的姿势，骄傲的展示着手中的武器。嵌着铆钉的拱门之间透出光芒，其内是由宝石碎片打造的马赛克窗格，展现着战斗和殉道的场景。那些结构完美的钻石和色彩斑斓的透镜，是从采矿激光和反应堆检查端口之中回收而来的。

展馆里挤满了身着传统手工服饰的卢德朝圣者，他们正在与圣地的圣务侍们会面。

texts.en: A robed subcurate shuffles to meet you. "Blessings upon you. Your arrival was... unexpected," they say. "But no matter. All who come in good faith are welcome to worship at this shrine."
